contracts.precondition: Rust FFI required to call C PJSUA library functions. Concurrency model defines reactor thread for serialized command execution.
contracts.postcondition: PJSIP FFI layer created with: (1) ffi::bindings module generated by bindgen build.rs with allowlist pattern, (2) PjOwnedStr safe wrapper for pj_str_t with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing, (3) extern C callback functions enqueue NativeEvent, (4) runtime/ modules use only safe SipBackend trait.
contracts.invariant: All unsafe code isolated to ffi/ module. No unsafe keyword in runtime/, client.rs, or config/. Compile-time lint enforces unsafe isolation.

contracts.precondition: PJSUA C library uses pj_pool_t for memory allocation. Callback parameters valid only within callback scope.
contracts.postcondition: pj_str_t always has Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>). Native callback pointers not held beyond callback scope. pj_pool_t memory never embedded in Rust structs.
contracts.invariant: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory. Original PJSUA ptr only used as source for immediate copy, never stored.

Source ticket P4-2 specified the audio format types, PairAligner, resampler and codec policy. During that implementation the build-time bindgen generation was left as stubs in build.rs and wrapper.h because PJSIP headers were not yet available in the build environment. This work item resolves those markers by generating PJSIP bindings via bindgen behind a new `pjsua-native` feature and uncommenting the wrapper.h includes once the headers are present.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Adding `pjsua-native` to the feature set with PJSIP headers available causes build.rs to run bindgen against wrapper.h and emit `pjsua_*` FFI declarations into OUT_DIR; `cargo build --features pjsua-native` succeeds and links.
【Happy path】build.rs resolves the PJSIP header root per RFC §28.1 search order (vendor/prebuilt/{target-triple}/include first, then vendor/pjsip source build) and passes wrapper.h to bindgen.
【Happy path】wrapper.h uncomments `#include <pjsua.h>`, `#include <pjmedia.h>`, and `#include <pjmedia-codec/opus.h>` when the `pjsua-native` feature is enabled.
【Happy path】The bindgen allowlist restricts generated declarations to the symbol subset siprs uses (pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pj_str_t, pjsua_call_get_info, etc.), keeping compile times low.
【Error case】With the feature disabled (default), the crate compiles with no bindgen and no PJSIP installation using the stub aliases in src/ffi/bindings.rs — the default build must not fail.

【Error case】With the feature enabled but headers/libraries missing, build.rs fails with a user-friendly error that names the missing dependency and references the RFC §28 per-OS package list — not a raw clang/bindgen error.

【Edge case】The generated bindings and the stub aliases are mutually exclusive: exactly one compiles depending on the feature flag; `check-cfg` lists `pjsua-native` so `cargo check` emits no unexpected-cfg warning.
【Invariant】No `unsafe` appears outside the ffi/ module after the build change (C038); build.rs itself contains no unsafe.

tickets.notes:
- Stub markers resolved: build.rs:8 (covers build.rs:8,11), wrapper.h:6.
- Implementation steps: 1) add `pjsua-native = []` to Cargo.toml [features] and `pjsua-native` to lints.rust check-cfg (line 40); 2) add `[build-dependencies]` bindgen (pin a version, e.g. bindgen = "0.69"); 3) implement build.rs main() per RFC §28: detect the feature via CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE, resolve the header root (vendor/prebuilt/{triple}/include → vendor/pjsip), run bindgen with the allowlist against wrapper.h, write to OUT_DIR; 4) uncomment the wrapper.h includes; 5) feature-gate src/ffi/bindings.rs stub aliases behind `#[cfg(not(feature = "pjsua-native"))]`.
- Related tickets: P3-2 (original FFI layer, contracts C038/C057), P8-18 (replace hand-coded PJSIP constants with bindgen output — consumes this ticket), P8-20 (wire real FFI call sites — consumes this ticket).
- Caveat: bindgen output varies by clang/bindgen version — the allowlist keeps the generated surface small and reviewable; pin the bindgen dependency in Cargo.toml. Verify with `make check-be` (default, stub path) and a feature-enabled build in a PJSIP-capable CI job.
tickets.invariants: 【C038】All unsafe code is isolated to the ffi/ module; no unsafe keyword appears in runtime/, client.rs, or config/ (compile-time enforced). 【C057】pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory (Vec<u8>); the original PJSUA pointer is used only as a source for immediate copy, never stored. 【Feature exclusivity】When `pjsua-native` is off, the crate builds with no external C library and no bindgen; when it is on, the bindgen-generated declarations replace the hand-written stubs exactly once — both are never compiled together. 【Build determinism】The bindgen allowlist is a fixed symbol set so generated output stays minimal and reviewable.
tickets.instrumentation:
- build.rs emits cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE and cargo:rerun-if-changed=wrapper.h so the script reruns when inputs change.
- build.rs prints which build path was taken (prebuilt / source-build / stub fallback) via println! so `cargo build -v` CI logs show the mode that produced the crate.
- When the feature is enabled but headers are missing, build.rs prints the RFC §28 package list to stderr with a `cargo:warning=` diagnostic so the failure reason is visible without a full build log.
tickets.investigation: build.rs:8-13 — `fn main()` is empty; lines 11-12 note 'feature and configure the wrapper.h header path once PJSIP is installed. The stub aliases in src/ffi/bindings.rs keep the crate compiling.' wrapper.h:6-10 — the three `#include` directives (`<pjsua.h>`, `<pjmedia.h>`, `<pjmedia-codec/opus.h>`) are commented out. Cargo.toml [features] (lines 15-37) declares no `pjsua-native` feature and there is no [build-dependencies] section, so `bindgen` is not available to build.rs; lints.rust check-cfg (line 40) lists only `cpal-input`. src/ffi/bindings.rs (lines 16-193) holds hand-written stub aliases (pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pj_str_t, pjsua_call_info) and a stub pjsua_call_get_info (lines 124-133) that keep the crate compiling without a PJSIP install; the module header comment (lines 3-6) already promises bindgen output replaces it under `pjsua-native`. RFC §28.1-§28.4 specify the build.rs search order (prebuilt → source build → bindgen) and per-OS package requirements. A real implementation must: add the feature, add bindgen to [build-dependencies], implement header-root resolution + allowlist + OUT_DIR emission, uncomment wrapper.h, and feature-gate the stub aliases so bindgen output replaces them only when the feature is enabled.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- The `[::STUB::]` comments in build.rs and wrapper.h are deleted once the real build script and includes are in place (no leftover STUB debris).
- bindgen allowlist symbols move into a named const array (e.g. BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST: &[&str]) so the symbol list reads as a declaration, not inline strings.
- build.rs functions are named as verb phrases matching RFC §28.2 pseudo-code: prebuilt_available(), emit_link_directives(), generate_bindings() — the flow reads top-to-bottom as prose.
- Error messages from build.rs use the RFC §28 package-list names verbatim so users can act on them.
- src/ffi/bindings.rs keeps the named constants PJ_SUCCESS/PJ_EUNKNOWN (already present) for any retained stub code; no new magic numbers.

[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]

Source ticket P1-3 specified the 4-layer test strategy, CI/CD pipeline, and panic policy. During that implementation the five example binaries were left as API-surface documentation stubs because the full CLI/PJSIP runtime was deferred — each example builds a ClientConfig, calls SipClient::new, and returns without performing its named operation. This work item resolves those markers by implementing the examples as runnable binaries with CLI args, real SipClient/PJSIP operations, and integration tests.
scope: Changes (path): examples/account_register.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args (host/port/username/domain/password), add an account, and register it per RFC §41.2
Changes (path): examples/audio_tap.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args, subscribe audio for a call, and stream AudioChunkPair frames per RFC §41.4
Changes (path): examples/client_init.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args and construct SipClient with transports/STUN per RFC §41.1
Changes (path): examples/make_call.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args (target URI), dial an OutgoingCallRequest, and wait for ring/connect events per RFC §41.3
Changes (path): examples/tts_source.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args, implement a real TtsStreamSource over mpsc, add it as an audio source, and set gain per RFC §41.5

Changes (path): Cargo.toml (MODIFY) — drop `autoexamples = false` and the `spec-examples` required-features gate once the referenced types exist; add the `cli` feature to the example builds if clap is used
Changes (path): tests/ (ADD) — Layer 5 integration tests that drive the example flows against MockBackend (contract C066)
Non-change (item): Removing the `spec-examples` feature declaration itself if some referenced types (SipClient, ClientConfig, AccountConfig) are still stubbed
Non-change (why): The example bodies depend on SipClient/account/call types that earlier tickets provide; the feature gate stays only until those exist
Impact (component): examples/ (5 binaries), Cargo.toml, tests/. The crate gains runnable reference clients for end users
Impact (nature): additive — examples compile behind their feature gate and are runnable via `cargo run --example <name>`
Impact (response): `make check-be` must still pass with the examples gated; integration tests run under `make test`
Out of scope: real PJSIP callback wiring inside SipClient (P5-3) and real microphone capture (P8-7) — examples consume the public API only

testExceptions: - Item: Running the examples against a live PJSIP/SIP endpoint (e.g. an actual PBX). Reason: needs a reachable SIP server and a real media path; the default `make test` environment uses MockBackend (Layer 2/5) and cannot assume a network SIP endpoint.

- Item: Real microphone capture in audio_tap. Reason: device capture requires the optional `cpal-input` feature (P8-7) and physical audio hardware; the example uses an injected source so it runs headless.

- Item: Verifying exact PJSIP call-state timing in make_call. Reason: ringing/connect timing depends on the live stack and network; integration tests assert event ordering with MockBackend, not wall-clock SIP behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Each of the five example binaries (account_register, audio_tap, client_init, make_call, tts_source) parses CLI args and runs against a real SipClient, performing its named operation instead of returning immediately.
【Happy path】account_register constructs an AccountConfig from CLI args and calls account.register(), exiting after registration completes or fails cleanly.
【Happy path】client_init constructs SipClient with transports/STUN per RFC §41.1 and reports the client capabilities.
【Happy path】make_call dials an OutgoingCallRequest to the CLI target URI and waits for OutgoingCallRinging / CallConnected / CallRejected events per RFC §41.3.
【Happy path】audio_tap subscribes to call audio via subscribe_audio and reads AudioChunkPair frames through AudioTapHandle::recv per RFC §41.4.
【Happy path】tts_source implements a TtsStreamSource (AsyncAudioSource over an mpsc receiver), adds it via add_audio_source, and sets gain per RFC §41.5.
【Error case】Each example exits non-zero with a user-facing error message when the SIP endpoint is unreachable, registration fails, or credentials are invalid — never panics.
【Edge case】Missing or invalid CLI args print a usage message to stderr and exit non-zero.
【Invariant】Every example main returns Result and propagates errors with `?`; no unwrap() in the example production paths (panic policy C056).

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】AudioTapMode is defined with exactly the Realtime and Lossless variants; Default == AudioTapMode::Realtime (RFC §22.1).
【Happy path】AudioTapHandle wraps a tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<AudioChunkPair> and `recv()` returns Option<AudioChunkPair>, yielding None when the sender closes.

【Happy path】The subscribe_audio entry point exists with the RFC §22 signature: subscribe_audio(call_id: CallId, format: AudioFormat, capacity: usize, mode: AudioTapMode) -> Result<AudioTapHandle, SipError>.

【Happy path】In Realtime mode, when the channel is full the oldest pair is dropped and the newest pair is preferred (oldest-drop), reporting an AudioTapOverflow condition — the audio pipeline is not blocked.
【Happy path】In Lossless mode, when the channel is full the producer side applies backpressure (blocks instead of dropping) so no pair is lost.
【Error case】subscribe_audio for an unknown call_id returns Err(SipError::not_found(...)) and does not create a handle.
【Edge case】capacity == 0 is rejected with Err(SipError) since a zero-capacity channel cannot carry a pair.
【Invariant】AudioTapMode is Clone + Copy + Debug + PartialEq + Eq; AudioTapHandle is Send and not Clone (a single consumer per tap).

tickets.invariants: 【C032】The Audio Subscribe API is available with a backpressure policy: Realtime is the default and never blocks the audio pipeline (oldest-drop + AudioTapOverflow report); Lossless is best-effort integrity that backpressures the producer and may induce jitter if the consumer is slow (RFC §22.1). 【C033】The tap consumes AudioChunkPair frames produced by AsyncAudioSource-driven media; the handle's receiver is single-consumer. 【Error handling】subscribe_audio never panics — unknown call_id and capacity == 0 return Err(SipError).
tickets.investigation: src/api/audio_subscribe_bp.rs — the file is a design-artifact shell: line 20 declares `pub trait Service {}` (unused placeholder) and line 23 carries the `[::STUB::]` marker. No AudioTapMode, AudioTapHandle, or subscribe_audio entry point exists anywhere in src/. The RFC §22 spec (lines 1368-1517) defines: AudioTapMode { Realtime (default), Lossless }, AudioTapHandle { rx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<AudioChunkPair> } with `recv() -> Option<AudioChunkPair>`, and `SipClient::subscribe_audio(call_id, format, capacity, mode) -> Result<AudioTapHandle, SipError>`. §22.1 specifies the backpressure policy: Realtime = oldest-drop + MediaError(AudioTapOverflow) with no pipeline impact; Lossless = producer-side backpressure in AudioWorkerTask with a best-effort integrity caveat. AudioChunkPair already exists in src/model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs (re-exported at lib.rs:106-111). A real implementation must define the enum + handle in this file and provide the subscribe_audio entry point (which may delegate to the SipClient/reactor once the backend exists).

- Remove the `pub trait Service {}` placeholder (audio_subscribe_bp.rs:20) — it is dead code unrelated to audio subscribe.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】After backend.send_dtmf succeeds, the reactor SendDtmf handler spawns spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout so a DtmfSent { method, digit, status: Err(SentDtmfError::Timeout), pjsip_status: None } event is published to the EventBus when no PJSIP completion callback arrives within DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】make_call() awaits the MakeCall reply and returns the CallId assigned by the backend reactor — the hardcoded Ok(1) at src/api/public_api_design.rs:142 is removed.
【Happy path】The returned CallId matches the CallEntry.id recorded in ClientState.calls (C046), so subsequent Hangup/Hold operate on a valid id.
【Error case】When the reactor replies Err(ReactorError), make_call() maps it to a SipError (e.g. SipErrorKind::InviteFailed) and does not fabricate a CallId.
【Error case】When the reply channel is dropped before sending, make_call() surfaces an error (oneshot recv failure) instead of returning a hardcoded value.

Source ticket P4-3 (Shutdown, Media Bridge, HTTP/WS Protocol & SQLite Schema) defined the SQLite accounts table and the standalone server mode (C065/C063). run_server() opens the DatabasePool but never restores persisted accounts, so saved accounts are not re-registered on startup. This work item resolves the marker by adding DatabasePool::load_accounts() and replaying each saved account through sip_client.add_account() at server startup.
scope: src/api/standalone_server_config.rs (run_server — load accounts from the pool and add each to sip_client before serving)
src/model/sqlite_schema.rs (DatabasePool::load_accounts() — query the accounts table into AccountEntity values)
src/client.rs (SipClient::add_account public method wrapping RuntimeCommand::AddAccount, if not already present)
src/runtime/command.rs (AddAccount dispatch — verify the reply path and account id)
Out of scope: the account persist/save path; full AccountEntity ↔ AccountConfig bijection beyond the read direction.
Impact: restarting the server re-registers all accounts saved in a previous run; feature-gated behind sqlite-storage.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] DatabasePool::load_accounts() on a temp DB returns the inserted AccountEntity rows.
UT: [Boundary] load_accounts() on an empty accounts table returns an empty Vec.
UT: [Error] load_accounts() propagates a DB error (e.g. missing table) as Err.
UT: [Normal] AccountEntity → AccountConfig mapping for the fields consumed by add_account.
UT: [Normal] The restoration loop calls add_account exactly once per loaded account (mock sip_client).
testIntegration: IT: [Server startup] Insert accounts into a temp DB, run the run_server restoration step, and verify sip_client.accounts() contains the restored accounts.
IT: [Fresh DB] run_server with an empty DB starts successfully with zero restored accounts.
testExceptions: Full registration against a live SIP registrar requires a network registrar and is not a unit-test concern. The restoration step (load + add_account) is testable with a temp SQLite DB and MockBackend.
The exact AccountEntity ↔ AccountConfig bijection depends on the persist path (out of scope); load_accounts only needs the read direction.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】run_server (sqlite-storage enabled) calls db.load_accounts() and calls sip_client.add_account() for each saved account before binding the listener.
【Happy path】DatabasePool::load_accounts() returns the rows of the accounts table as AccountEntity values; an empty table yields an empty Vec.
【Error case】A DB error from load_accounts() surfaces as a startup SipError rather than silently starting with no accounts.
【Edge case】A fresh/empty accounts table starts the server with zero accounts and no error.

【Edge case】Each AccountEntity maps to an AccountConfig (username, domain, transport, register_on_start, display_name) so the restored account is equivalent to the persisted one; an account that fails add_account is logged and skipped rather than aborting startup.
No account restoration occurs when the sqlite-storage feature is disabled.

This work item resolves it by implementing PJSIP build detection, feature-flag configuration (pjsua-native, tls, srtp), and a build/CI entry point that exercises both with-PJSIP and without-PJSIP builds.
scope: - src/build/build_strategy_os_deps.rs:27,32 — replace the no-op fn main() {} entry point with real PJSIP build detection
- src/build/mod.rs — export the new build-strategy module and its entry point
- src/build/cicd_docker_prebuilt.rs — consume the CI matrix (CiOsTarget, FeatureCombination) against detection results
- build.rs — coordinate PJSIP header/library detection with the pjsua-native feature (currently a P8-5 bindgen stub)
- Cargo.toml — declare the pjsua-native feature and wire tls/srtp flags from detection
- Out of scope: bindgen binding generation (P8-5); runtime FFI call sites (P8-20); callback registration (P8-21).
- Impact: cargo build / CI matrix for the crate; feature-gated config types (TransportConfig::Tls, ClientCapabilities.tls_available/srtp_available).
testUnit: UT: [Normal] build detection returns Present{version} when the detection backend reports a known PJSIP version
UT: [Normal] detection maps present PJSIP to the pjsua-native feature and absent PJSIP to the stub-alias fallback path
UT: [Boundary] the feature-combination enumeration covers all 4 combinations from cicd_docker_prebuilt.rs (Default, Tls, Srtp, TlsSrtp) with the correct flag sets
UT: [Error] detection on an unsupported OS returns a structured error instead of panicking
testIntegration: IT: cargo build --no-default-features succeeds without a PJSIP install (stub-alias path stays green)
IT: cargo build --features tls,srtp succeeds when detection reports TLS/SRTP libraries present
testExceptions: Real PJSIP installation/version detection depends on the build environment and cannot run in a pure unit test; unit tests drive a mock detection backend. Full CI matrix execution requires GitHub Actions runners — local tests verify the matrix enumeration and runner labels, not actual remote runs.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】A build-detection routine in build_strategy_os_deps.rs detects a system PJSIP installation and returns a typed result (present with version, or absent).
【Happy path】The detection result maps to Cargo feature flags: PJSIP present enables the pjsua-native feature path; tls/srtp flags are set from detected libraries.
【Happy path】The build/CI entry point runs without panicking on both present and absent PJSIP, printing actionable diagnostics (e.g., "PJSIP not found — install pjsua2 or use the prebuilt pipeline").
【Error case】Detection failure (unsupported OS, missing pkg-config/headers) produces a structured error or non-zero exit code — it never silently passes.
【Edge case】The CI matrix (windows-latest/macos-14/ubuntu-22.04 × Default/Tls/Srtp/TlsSrtp from cicd_docker_prebuilt.rs) enumerates every feature combination and reports per-combination status.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) specified the codec policy but left runtime enumeration deferred. The marker at src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69 was left as a stub because the FFI-defined pjsua_codec_info types are not generated until bindgen runs under the pjsua-native feature. This work item resolves it by replacing the placeholder codec list and Codec type with runtime codec enumeration via the PJSIP codec API.
scope: - src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69,187 — replace the available_codecs: Vec<Codec> placeholder and the Codec struct with FFI-backed enumeration
- src/ffi/bindings.rs — consume the bindgen-generated pjsua_codec_info type once pjsua-native is enabled
- src/ffi/mod.rs — expose the codec-enumeration FFI surface (pjsua_enum_codecs path)
- Out of scope: PairAligner/resampler pipeline (C036/C037); codec policy/negotiation internals (C041/C042) beyond what enumeration feeds.
- Impact: ClientCapabilities.available_codecs, ClientCapabilities.opus_available, and every caller reading codec capability.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] maps a pjsua_codec_info fixture (id="opus", clock_rate=48000) to Codec { id, name, clock_rate }
UT: [Normal] opus_available is true when the enumerated list contains "opus" and false otherwise
UT: [Boundary] an empty enumeration yields an empty available_codecs and opus_available=false
UT: [Error] an enumeration FFI error returns an empty list with a logged diagnostic and no panic
testIntegration: IT: With pjsua-native enabled, ClientCapabilities::new() reflects the real codec set; with it disabled, available_codecs is empty.
testExceptions: Real codec enumeration requires a linked PJSIP library (pjsua_enum_codecs), so unit tests use a fixed pjsua_codec_info fixture — the live call is environment-dependent. Only the three Codec fields (id, name, clock_rate) are modelled and asserted; other pjsua_codec_info fields are out of scope.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】ClientCapabilities.available_codecs is populated from a real pjsua codec enumeration when pjsua-native is enabled, mapping each pjsua_codec_info entry to Codec { id, name, clock_rate }.
【Happy path】ClientCapabilities.opus_available reflects whether the enumerated codecs contain "opus".
【Error case】When enumeration fails (no PJSIP link, FFI error), available_codecs degrades to an empty list rather than panicking, and the failure is logged.
【Edge case】A one-to-one mapping test converts a fixed pjsua_codec_info fixture (id, name, clock_rate) to Codec.
【Edge case】Without pjsua-native, the fallback path still yields an empty available_codecs and the crate compiles without PJSIP.
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P5-2 (depends on: AudioMixer uses audio format types), P2-3 (depends on: event system uses AudioChunk), P7 (depends on: audio subscribe uses AudioChunkPair)
tickets.notes: Stub sites: src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69,187. Depends on P8-5 (bindgen generates pjsua_codec_info) and P8-16 (pjsua-native feature flag). Implementation: (1) add Codec::from_pjsua_codec_info; (2) add the FFI codec-enumeration function under pjsua-native; (3) call it when populating ClientCapabilities; (4) keep the empty-list fallback for the non-feature path. Related: P8-18 (PJSIP constants).
tickets.invariants: Codec auto mode must assign Opus=255 and PCMU=254 invariantly (C042). Codec policy only accepts PCMU and Opus (C041) — enumeration may report more codecs, but policy filtering still restricts to PCMU/Opus. Every enumerated Codec has a non-empty id and clock_rate > 0. available_codecs is derived from enumeration, never hand-maintained — no hardcoded codec list remains.
tickets.instrumentation: Add tracing::info! on enumeration success with the codec count, and tracing::warn! on enumeration failure. Consider a 'codecs.enumerated' counter metric.
tickets.investigation: src/config/observability_metrics.rs declares ClientCapabilities.available_codecs: Vec<Codec> at line 69, ClientCapabilities::new() initializes it to Vec::new(), and the Codec struct at lines 187-196 is { id: String, name: String, clock_rate: u32 } — a pure placeholder with no FFI backing (the marker covers :69 and :187). ffi/bindings.rs currently provides only stub type aliases (pjsua_acc_id = i32, pjsua_call_id = i32, pjsua_conf_port_id = i32, pjsua_transport_id = i32) and a minimal pjsua_call_info mirror — there is no pjsua_codec_info yet (that arrives with the P8-5 bindgen work). A real implementation must add a codec-enumeration FFI surface (pjsua_enum_codecs / pjsua_codec_info), map each entry into Codec, populate available_codecs and opus_available, and keep the non-pjsua-native path compiling with an empty list.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the placeholder comment above Codec once it has a real from_pjsua_codec_info conversion. Extract the mapping as a named conversion function so the enumeration loop reads as prose. Document the empty-list fallback in ClientCapabilities::new() instead of leaving it unexplained.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) introduced PJSIP-native state mapping, but the PJSUA/PJSIP numeric constants were hand-copied from pjsua.h. These markers were left as stubs because the bindgen-generated constants from pjsua.h are not available until the pjsua-native feature enables FFI. This work item resolves them by replacing the hand-coded constants with the bindgen-generated constants.
scope: - src/error/error_design_siperror.rs:32 — replace hand-coded PJ_SUCCESS/PJ_ENOMEM/PJ_EINVALIDOP/PJ_EBUSY consts consumed by convert_pj_status
- src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs:32 — replace hand-coded PJ_SUCCESS/PJ_EINVALIDOP consumed by the M20 error converters
- src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:59,70 — replace hand-coded pjsip_inv_state and pjsua_call_media_status modules
- src/ffi/bindings.rs — expose the bindgen-generated constants under pjsua-native; keep stub aliases otherwise
- Out of scope: SipErrorKind semantics; call-state conversion logic beyond the constant source.
- Impact: convert_pj_status, convert_call_state, convert_call_media_state, and every M20 native_error_with_status caller.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] convert_pj_status maps PJ_SUCCESS to None and PJ_EINVALIDOP to NativeError using the bindgen constants
UT: [Normal] convert_call_state maps pjsip_inv_state::CONFIRMED to CallConnected and DISCONNECTED to CallDisconnected
UT: [Normal] convert_call_media_state maps pjsua_call_media_status values (ACTIVE, LOCAL_HOLD, REMOTE_HOLD, ERROR) to CallMediaState
UT: [Boundary] pjsip_inv_state::NULL yields None (no event published)
UT: [Error] an unknown state value falls through to None without panicking
testIntegration: IT: A full build with pjsua-native enabled compiles, and the call/error mapping tests pass against the bindgen-generated constants.
testExceptions: The bindgen-generated constants only exist under pjsua-native with a real PJSIP install; unit tests assert behavior through the mapping functions, which is identical under both constant sources. The exact numeric values are owned by pjsua.h/bindgen — this ticket asserts mapping behavior, not the numeric values.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】With pjsua-native enabled, error_design_siperror.rs, m20_runtime_command_error.rs, and m20_callstate_mapping.rs reference the bindgen-generated constants (PJ_SUCCESS, PJ_EINVALIDOP, PJSUA_CALL_* / pjsua_call_media_status) with no hand-coded duplicate values.
【Happy path】convert_pj_status / convert_call_state / convert_call_media_state produce identical outputs to the previous hand-coded values for the same inputs (behavior regression preserved).
【Error case】A constant missing from the bindgen output causes a compile error — there is no silent fallback to a hardcoded value.
【Edge case】Without pjsua-native, the ffi::bindings stub aliases keep the crate compiling and the mapping functions still work against the stub constants.

tickets.notes: Stub sites: src/error/error_design_siperror.rs:32, src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs:32, src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:59,70. Depends on P8-5 (bindgen output) and P8-16 (pjsua-native feature). Implementation: (1) expose the bindgen constants from ffi::bindings under pjsua-native; (2) replace the local consts with ffi::bindings references; (3) keep stub aliases for the non-feature path; (4) keep the mapping tests green. Related: P8-17 (codec enumeration), P8-20 (FFI call sites).
tickets.invariants: No PJSIP/PJSUA numeric constant is hand-coded in src/error or src/state — every value comes from ffi::bindings (bindgen under pjsua-native, stub aliases otherwise). Codec auto mode must assign Opus=255 and PCMU=254 invariantly (C042). Codec policy only accepts PCMU and Opus (C041).
tickets.instrumentation: No new runtime metrics required. Add a compile-time assertion that the mapping functions still compile when the constant source switches to bindgen.
tickets.investigation: Three files hand-code PJSUA constants. error_design_siperror.rs:32 defines const PJ_SUCCESS: i32 = 0, PJ_ENOMEM: i32 = -2, PJ_EINVALIDOP: i32 = 150002, PJ_EBUSY, consumed by convert_pj_status (lines 300-306). m20_runtime_command_error.rs:32 defines PJ_SUCCESS = 0 and PJ_EINVALIDOP = 150002, consumed by convert_conf_disconnect_error and native_error_with_status (lines 40-50). m20_callstate_mapping.rs:59-70 defines pjsip_inv_state { NULL=0, CALLING=1, CONNECTING=2, CONFIRMED=3, DISCONNECTED=4 } and pjsua_call_media_status { NONE=0, ACTIVE=1, LOCAL_HOLD=2, REMOTE_HOLD=3, ERROR=4 }, used by convert_call_state and convert_call_media_state. ffi/bindings.rs currently carries stub aliases (PJ_SUCCESS=0, PJ_EUNKNOWN=-1, PJSUA_CALL_NULL..PJSUA_CALL_DISCONNECTED=0..6, PJSUA_REG_STATE_*) and will be replaced by bindgen output under pjsua-native. The real implementation must route the three files through ffi::bindings constants and delete the local duplicate const blocks.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Delete the duplicated const blocks and route every reference through ffi::bindings so there is a single source of truth. Remove the 'hand-coded duplicates of pjsua.h' comments. Consolidate the PJ_SUCCESS/PJ_EINVALIDOP imports shared by error_design_siperror.rs and m20_runtime_command_error.rs onto one source.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P5-1 (Raw SIP Message, Call API & Audio Subscribe) specified the event model and call API. The markers at src/error/error_design_siperror.rs:204 and src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs:115 were left as stubs because the error fields still use raw i32/u64 where AccountId/CallId newtypes already exist in the event model but callers are not yet migrated. This work item resolves them by migrating the error fields (and AccountInfo) to the AccountId/CallId newtypes once the newtypes are stable across callers.
scope: - src/error/error_design_siperror.rs:204 — SipError.account_id: Option<u64> → Option<AccountId>, call_id: Option<u64> → Option<CallId>
- src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs:115 — AccountInfo.account_id: u64 → AccountId
- src/model/id_design_newtype.rs — the AccountId/CallId newtypes (NonZeroU64, from_u64)
- All SipError construction sites: SipError::new, native_error_with_status, convert_get_account_info_error, ReactorError::from, plus every in-crate caller that sets or matches account_id/call_id
- Out of scope: the reactor account state machine (P8-12) that delivers real AccountInfo values.
- Impact: every caller constructing or matching SipError / AccountInfo.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] SipError::new produces account_id: None and call_id: None with the newtype field types
UT: [Normal] native_error_with_status preserves native_status and leaves account_id/call_id as None
UT: [Boundary] converting a native acc_id of 0 (sentinel) via AccountId::from_u64 yields None and the error omits the id
UT: [Boundary] a valid non-zero native id converts to Some(AccountId) and round-trips to the same u64
UT: [Error] the account-not-found error path returns AccountNotFound with account_id None — no u64 leaks into the error
testIntegration: IT: A MakeCall failure flows through the reactor to a SipError whose call_id is a CallId newtype, and the caller can match on it without raw u64.
testExceptions: Full caller migration spans the whole call/account API surface; unit tests cover the error type and its converters, while integration tests cover reactor-to-API propagation. Real AccountInfo values still depend on P8-12 (reactor account state machine) — this ticket changes the types, not the retrieval.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】SipError carries account_id: Option<AccountId> and call_id: Option<CallId> (newtypes), and AccountInfo.account_id is AccountId — no u64 ID fields remain in these types.
【Happy path】SipError::new / native_error_with_status compile with the newtype fields and default account_id/call_id to None.
【Error case】A native id of 0 (PJSUA invalid sentinel) converts to None via AccountId::from_u64 / CallId::from_u64 — never a panic and never a stored 0.
【Edge case】All in-crate callers that set account_id/call_id are migrated to construct the newtypes from the native u32/u64 via from_u64, dropping the 0 sentinel.
【Edge case】The stub markers are removed only after the type migration compiles and the full test suite passes.

Implementation: (1) change SipError.account_id/call_id to Option<AccountId>/Option<CallId>; (2) change AccountInfo.account_id to AccountId; (3) update all constructors and callers; (4) keep the 0-sentinel → None rule. The PJSUA 0 sentinel always maps to None at the FFI boundary; it is never stored as a valid identifier. Answer semantics and call-state invariants from the call API remain unchanged by the type migration (C028). SipError keeps exactly its 6 public fields with Send + Sync preserved.

tickets.instrumentation: Add a tracing::warn! (or debug_assert!) when a 0 native id is dropped to None during conversion, aiding sentinel diagnostics.
tickets.investigation: SipError (error_design_siperror.rs:180-206) has six public fields including native_status: Option<i32>, account_id: Option<u64>, call_id: Option<u64>; the marker at :204 flags the u64 fields as pending AccountId/CallId migration. AccountId and CallId already exist as NonZeroU64-backed newtypes re-exported via event_model_payload_bus.rs:29-32 (pub use crate::model::AccountId / CallId) and are already used by the event model (RegistrationInfo.account_id, ConnectedCallInfo.call_id) and by m20_callstate_mapping::convert_call_state via CallId::from_u64. AccountInfo (m20_runtime_command_error.rs:107-116) still uses account_id: u64. Construction sites include SipError::new, native_error_with_status (m20_runtime_command_error.rs:40-50), convert_get_account_info_error (which also carries a P8-12 stub returning placeholder AccountInfo), and ReactorError::from. Migration must update all of these and their callers, mapping native u32/u64 ids through AccountId::from_u64 / CallId::from_u64 and dropping the 0 sentinel to None.

The markers at src/ffi/bindings.rs:123, src/runtime/backend.rs:287, and src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs:110 were left as stubs because the pjsua-native feature and library linkage are not ready. This work item resolves them by replacing the canned/unimplemented FFI call sites with real bindgen-generated calls and obtaining actual media_status.
scope: - src/ffi/bindings.rs:123 — replace the canned pjsua_call_get_info stub with the real bindgen call; extend pjsua_call_info to the full bindgen struct (conf_slot + media_status)
- src/runtime/backend.rs:287 — implement PjsuaBackend methods against real PJSUA FFI instead of Err(BackendError("unimplemented"))
- src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs:110 — call the real pjsua_call_get_info to obtain actual media_status instead of hardcoding 1
- Out of scope: build detection/feature flags (P8-16); bindgen generation (P8-5); callback registration (P8-21).
- Impact: CallMediaStateChanged event accuracy; PjsuaBackend call/registration/media operations.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] convert_call_media_state maps media_status values (0=NONE, 1=ACTIVE, 2/3=LOCAL/REMOTE_HOLD, 4=ERROR) to CallMediaState
UT: [Normal] a real pjsua_call_get_info result (fixture) sets both conf_slot and media_status on the info struct
UT: [Error] pjsua_call_get_info returning non-PJ_SUCCESS produces a BackendError carrying the status
UT: [Edge] an unknown/absent media_status maps to a safe default (CallMediaState::Error) rather than panicking
testIntegration: IT: An incoming call's media event flows callback → NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged → real pjsua_call_get_info → CallMediaState, without the hardcoded media_status=1.
IT: PjsuaBackend::hangup / make_call propagate real PJSUA return codes into ReactorError.
testExceptions: Real FFI calls require PJSIP library linkage (pjsua-native + linked lib); unit tests use a fixture/mock for pjsua_call_get_info because the real symbol is unavailable in the sandbox. End-to-end media_status accuracy depends on a live PJSIP call — the event-conversion path is unit-tested with fixture media_status values.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Under pjsua-native, pjsua_call_get_info invokes the real FFI symbol and fills conf_slot and media_status from the actual pjsua_call_info struct.
【Happy path】NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged converts the real media_status from pjsua_call_get_info into CallMediaState (Active/Held/Error) — no hardcoded 1.
【Happy path】PjsuaBackend methods (make_call, answer_call, hangup, conf_connect, etc.) call real PJSUA functions and return their actual status.
【Error case】A non-success PJSUA status from a real FFI call maps to Err(ReactorError::BackendError) with the diagnostic preserved — never a canned success.
【Edge case】Without pjsua-native, the stub aliases remain so the crate compiles; the real-call path is feature-gated.
【Edge case】The canned-value tests in bindings.rs are replaced by tests asserting the real-call wiring (or are feature-gated).

Depends on P8-5 (bindgen output incl. full pjsua_call_info) and P8-16 (pjsua-native feature + linkage). Implementation: (1) replace the pjsua_call_get_info stub with the real call under pjsua-native; (2) extend pjsua_call_info with media_status; (3) wire m20_native_event_conv to read the real media_status; (4) implement the PjsuaBackend methods; (5) keep the non-feature stub path. Related: P8-18 (constants), P8-21 (callbacks).
tickets.invariants: The media_status reported for a call always comes from pjsua_call_get_info — never a hardcoded constant. Every PjsuaBackend method returns Err on a non-zero PJSUA status; a canned Ok(()) for an unexecuted FFI call is prohibited. Audio delivery keeps IN/OUT paired by timestamp (C031); codec policy remains PCMU and Opus only (C041); auto mode assigns Opus=255 and PCMU=254 (C042).
tickets.instrumentation: Add tracing::warn! on non-success PJSUA status at the FFI boundary. Expose a counter for CallMediaStateChanged events with their mapped media status.
tickets.investigation: ffi/bindings.rs:110-134 defines a minimal pjsua_call_info mirror containing only conf_slot and a stub pjsua_call_get_info that writes conf_slot = call_id and returns PJ_SUCCESS — canned values; its tests assert the canned behavior (conf_slot must match call_id). m20_native_event_conv.rs:104-113 handles NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged by calling convert_call_media_state(cid, 1) — media_status hardcoded to 1 (ACTIVE) because the real pjsua_call_get_info is not wired. runtime/backend.rs:287+ defines PjsuaBackend (derives Default) whose SipBackend methods (set_registration, make_call, answer_call, hangup, send_dtmf, configure_codecs, transfer_call, shutdown, conf_connect, conf_disconnect) all return Err(ReactorError::BackendError("... not yet implemented (P4-2)")). A real implementation must gate these on pjsua-native, invoke the bindgen FFI symbols, propagate status codes, and obtain actual media_status for CallMediaStateChanged.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the canned pjsua_call_get_info body and the test asserting conf_slot == call_id. Extract a resolve_media_status helper used by the CallMediaStateChanged path. Replace the per-method Err("... not yet implemented (P4-2)") boilerplate in PjsuaBackend with real calls, deleting the stub strings.

testExceptions: Live PJSIP callback invocation requires a linked PJSIP and a running account/call; unit tests invoke the extern "C" functions directly with synthetic args. The exact pjsua_config.cb field names are bindgen-dependent — the registration helper is asserted for the set of callback pointers, not the C layout.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Each PJSIP callback is registered into pjsua_config.cb and, when invoked, enqueues a NativeEvent (on_incoming_call → CallStateChanged, on_reg_state → RegistrationStateChanged, on_call_media_state → CallMediaStateChanged, on_dtmf_digit → DtmfDigit, on_reg_started → RegistrationStarted, on_call_redirected → CallRedirected, on_call_transfer_status → CallTransferStatus).

【Happy path】The enqueue uses only the permitted operations — copy params into a pre-allocated NativeEvent and push on a lock-free queue / MPSC — with no locks, allocation, .await, or PJSUA re-entry (design constraint in callback.rs:6-14).
【Error case】When the queue is full, the enqueue is loss-tolerant (event dropped, counter incremented) — it never blocks the PJSIP real-time thread.

【Edge case】The P1/P2 NativeEvent variants that currently return None in convert_native_event_to_payload (CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected) are now produced by their callbacks and either converted or explicitly deferred with a documented reason.
【Edge case】The stub markers are removed only after the callbacks enqueue real events and the reactor round-trip tests pass.

Implementation: (1) add register_callbacks(pjsua_config, channel); (2) implement each callback to enqueue a NativeEvent; (3) use a pre-allocated lock-free queue / MPSC per the design constraints; (4) update convert_native_event_to_payload for the newly produced variants; (5) keep the no-op stub path behind !pjsua-native. tickets.invariants: Callbacks never allocate, lock, await, or call back into PJSUA (design constraint from callback.rs:6-14). NativeEvent enqueue is loss-tolerant: a full queue drops the event and increments a counter, never blocking. Audio delivery keeps IN/OUT paired by timestamp (C031); codec policy remains PCMU and Opus only (C041); auto mode assigns Opus=255 and PCMU=254 (C042).
tickets.instrumentation: Add a monotonic counter for enqueued NativeEvents and a separate counter for dropped events on queue-full. tracing::debug! on callback entry with call_id/acc_id only (no payload copy).
tickets.investigation: ffi/callback.rs declares #[no_mangle] unsafe extern "C" callbacks — on_incoming_call (:16), on_reg_state (:30), on_call_state (:51), on_call_media_state (:74), plus on_reg_started / on_call_redirected / on_dtmf_digit / on_call_transfer_status (covers :91,97 per the marker) — each currently discards its arguments (let _ = (...)): pure no-ops. The design-constraint comment (callback.rs:6-14) mandates copying event params into a pre-allocated NativeEvent and enqueueing on a lock-free queue or MPSC channel. ffi/mod.rs:27 documents the callback module; there is no register_callbacks entry point yet. m20_native_event_conv.rs declares the NativeEvent variants (RegistrationStateChanged, RegistrationStarted, CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfDigit, plus P1/P2 TransportStateChanged, IceTransportError, CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected) but convert_native_event_to_payload returns None for the P1/P2 variants. The real implementation must (1) register the callbacks in pjsua_config.cb, (2) enqueue NativeEvents via a lock-free / MPSC channel, (3) let the reactor drain and convert, and (4) decide P1/P2 conversion or document deferral.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the let _ = (...) no-op bodies and replace them with a shared enqueue_native_event helper used by every callback (single source of truth for the lock-free enqueue). Delete the stale doc comments claiming the callbacks are no-ops. Ensure the channel is pre-allocated at registration time to honor the no-allocation rule.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P3-1 specified the public API surface for account and transport configuration (AccountConfig validation, TransportConfig/ICE). The src/lib.rs:51 stub deferred the account/call/transport lifecycle methods because the configuration types (AccountConfig, TransportConfig, OutgoingCallRequest) were not yet stable enough to wire through RuntimeCommand dispatch. This work item resolves the deferred lifecycle by implementing the account and transport configuration lifecycle methods - creating (add), modifying (update_config), and deleting (remove) accounts, plus transport configuration methods.
scope: - src/lib.rs - replace the P8-22 stub at line 51; keep account/call/transport module declarations
- src/client.rs - SipClient::add_account / remove_account facade methods
- src/api/public_api_design.rs - SipAccountHandle lifecycle: real update_config (replaces the P8-14 no-op), remove, and transport methods
- src/runtime/command.rs - RuntimeCommand variants for account modify/delete and transport configuration
- src/runtime/reactor.rs - dispatch the new account/transport lifecycle commands
- src/config/account_config_spec.rs - AccountConfig validation reused for the modify path
- src/config/transport_ice_spec.rs - TransportConfig types wired into the transport lifecycle
- src/transport.rs - re-export/verify transport config types

- Out of scope: SipCall lifecycle (make/answer/hangup/hold/transfer/send_dtmf) is covered by P8-9; Audio Subscribe by P8-8; registration-state retrieval by P8-12; startup account restoration by P8-15.
- Impact: public API surface for account/transport lifecycle; RuntimeCommand gains new variants; SipClient/SipAccountHandle stay Clone + Send + Sync.
testUnit: UT: [C012] SipClient::add_account submits RuntimeCommand::AddAccount (asserted via MockBackend call records).
UT: [C012] SipClient::remove_account submits RuntimeCommand::RemoveAccount with the correct account_id.
UT: [C015] add_account rejects AccountConfig with empty username with Err(InvalidConfig) before dispatch.
UT: [C052] add_account rejects AccountCodecPolicy with both enable_pcmu=false and enable_opus=false.
UT: [C052] update_config with an invalid patch returns Err(InvalidConfig) and leaves the stored account unchanged.
UT: [C016] TransportConfig UDP/TCP variants construct and round-trip; the TLS variant compiles only with the tls feature.
UT: [C017] All lifecycle methods return Result<T, SipError> (compile-time signature assertions).
UT: [Normal] add_account with all-Optional-fields-None AccountConfig succeeds (display_name=None, auth_username=None, registrar_uri=None, outbound_proxy=[], contact_params=[]).
UT: [Boundary] remove_account of the same account twice: the second call returns Err (not found), no panic.
UT: [Error] update_config/remove_account on a non-existent account_id returns Err.
testIntegration: IT: [Lifecycle] add_account -> accounts() shows the account -> update_config changes stored config -> remove_account removes it, verified via the reactor's authoritative ClientState (read().await).
IT: [Validation-before-dispatch] MockBackend records zero add_account calls when an invalid AccountConfig is submitted.
IT: [Concurrency] Add and remove accounts from multiple tokio tasks; FIFO order preserved through the MPSC channel (C011).
testExceptions: Actual PJSUA registration/transport binding requires a running PJSIP stack (pjsua-native feature), which is not available in unit tests; MockBackend/PjsuaBackend stubs are used instead.
TLS compile-time gating is verified via cargo check with/without the tls feature, not by runtime unit tests.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】SipClient::add_account(AccountConfig) validates the config, submits RuntimeCommand::AddAccount, and returns a SipAccountHandle with a non-zero account_id on success.
【Happy path】SipAccountHandle::update_config(patch) submits an account-modify command and applies validated changes without dropping or recreating the account.
【Happy path】SipClient::remove_account(account_id) submits RuntimeCommand::RemoveAccount; the account no longer appears in accounts().
【Happy path】Transport configuration (UDP/TCP/ICE via TransportConfig) is accepted and reflected in the reactor's transport runtime state.
【Error case】add_account with an invalid AccountConfig returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig) before any RuntimeCommand is submitted - no state mutation on validation failure.
【Error case】update_config/remove_account on a non-existent account_id returns Err (InvalidConfig or NotInitialized), never panics.
【Edge case】AccountConfig with register_on_start=false and allow_outbound_without_register=true validates successfully and can be added.
【Edge case】All lifecycle methods are async fn returning Result<T, SipError>; SipClient/SipAccountHandle remain Clone + Send + Sync.

tickets.notes:
- Stub file:line list - src/lib.rs:51.
- Implementation steps: (1) add SipClient::add_account/remove_account facades; (2) implement real update_config and transport methods; (3) add RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount and transport variants; (4) wire reactor dispatch; (5) Red tests, then Green.
- Dependencies: RuntimeCommand already has AddAccount/RemoveAccount/SetRegistration (command.rs:49-56) backed by SipBackend trait methods (backend.rs:31-38); reuse AccountConfig validation from account_config_spec.rs.
- Related tickets: P8-9 (SipCall lifecycle), P8-13 (real CallId), P8-14 (update_config), P8-12 (account info), P8-15 (startup account restoration).
tickets.invariants:
- All account/transport lifecycle API functions return Result<T, SipError> (C017). Validation failures return Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig) before any RuntimeCommand submission - no partial state mutation.
- AccountConfig validation enforces non-empty username/domain/password, at least one enabled codec, and non-empty send/receive method lists (C015, C052).
- TransportConfig TLS variant is gated by #[cfg(feature = "tls")] and never present at runtime without the feature (C016, C043).
- Registration lifecycle (register/unregister) remains independent of call ability (C026).
- Codec policy only accepts PCMU and Opus (C041).
- SipClient is Clone, Send, Sync; RuntimeHandle is never leaked outside the crate.
tickets.instrumentation:
- #[instrument(skip(self))] on SipClient::add_account/remove_account and SipAccountHandle lifecycle methods, logging account_id and a config summary.
- tracing::info! for successful add/remove/transport lifecycle transitions; tracing::warn! on validation rejection with the violated rule.
tickets.investigation:
- src/lib.rs:49-55 declares `pub mod account; pub mod call; pub mod transport;` under the P8-22 stub at line 51 ("account/call/transport lifecycle methods are deferred"). account.rs (lines 1-8) and transport.rs (lines 1-21) are pure re-export modules; call.rs:13-22 holds the SipCall placeholder covered by P8-9.
- src/api/public_api_design.rs:31-37 defines SipAccountHandle. It has register/unregister/set_registration_enabled (submit RuntimeCommand::SetRegistration), registration_state (line 116 returns Idle - P8-12's stub), make_call (line 123 returns hardcoded 1 - P8-13's stub), and update_config (line 150 returns Ok(()) - P8-14's no-op stub).
- src/client.rs exposes new/subscribe/accounts/call_state/is_terminated/shutdown but has NO add_account/remove_account facade methods yet; account add/remove exist only on the SipBackend trait (src/runtime/backend.rs:31,38) and RuntimeCommand::AddAccount/RemoveAccount (src/runtime/command.rs:49-56).
- What a real implementation must provide: SipClient::add_account/remove_account facades that validate AccountConfig then submit RuntimeCommand; a real SipAccountHandle::update_config dispatch; transport configuration lifecycle methods; RuntimeCommand update-account/transport variants and their reactor dispatch; all returning Result<T, SipError> and never mutating state on validation failure.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Replace the manual oneshot plumbing in SipAccountHandle (public_api_design.rs lines 55, 75, 95, 131 create (_tx,_rx) and immediately drop) with the crate's send_reply-style helper or a shared submit helper to eliminate dead channels.
- Remove #[allow(dead_code)] from any field that becomes read by the new lifecycle methods.
- Add #[instrument] on every new public method, matching the existing pattern enforced at client.rs:720.

contracts.precondition: Tokio async runtime must be initialized (tokio::runtime::Handle::current() succeeds). AudioWorkerTask must be spawned on Tokio blocking pool via tokio::task::spawn_blocking.
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer struct created with lock-free queue boundary: crossbeam::ArrayQueue<Vec<i16>> out_queue separates AudioWorkerTask (async context) from RustMediaPort (PJSIP RT callback context). AudioWorkerTask runs process_frame loop in blocking pool.
contracts.invariant: No blocking operations (lock acquisition, dynamic memory allocation, syscall, .await) are permitted inside any function called from PJSIP RT callback thread (get_frame/put_frame). Only lock-free queue pop/push, memcpy, and zero-fill are allowed.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit validates: AudioMixer::new() creates struct with empty crossbeam::ArrayQueue. AudioWorkerTask::spawn succeeds when called from tokio::test context.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit validates: AudioWorkerTask::process_frame pushes mixed frame to out_queue. Mixer entry push operation does not panic.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit validates: crossbeam::ArrayQueue push from std::thread does not deadlock or panic. memcpy within callback context verified via mock port struct.

contracts.precondition: Rust FFI required to call C PJSUA library functions. Concurrency model defines reactor thread for serialized command execution.
contracts.postcondition: PJSIP FFI layer created with: (1) ffi::bindings module generated by bindgen build.rs with allowlist pattern, (2) PjOwnedStr safe wrapper for pj_str_t with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing, (3) extern C callback functions enqueue NativeEvent, (4) runtime/ modules use only safe SipBackend trait.
contracts.invariant: All unsafe code isolated to ffi/ module. No unsafe keyword in runtime/, client.rs, or config/. Compile-time lint enforces unsafe isolation.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit: build.rs must exist with allowlist patterns. ffi::bindings module references pjsua_* types at compile time.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit: PjOwnedStr::new creates pj_str_t with ptr pointing to owned Vec<u8>. extern C callback compiles without panic.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit via compile-time: runtime/ directory grep for 'unsafe' returns 0 matches (excluding test code).

contracts.precondition: PJSUA C library uses pj_pool_t for memory allocation. Callback parameters valid only within callback scope.
contracts.postcondition: pj_str_t always has Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>). Native callback pointers not held beyond callback scope. pj_pool_t memory never embedded in Rust structs.
contracts.invariant: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory. Original PJSUA ptr only used as source for immediate copy, never stored.
contracts.testPrecondition: Deferred to P4-2/P5-2. P3-2 verifies only that PjOwnedStr ensures Rust-ownership.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit: PjOwnedStr::new copies input bytes to owned Vec<u8>. Dropping PjOwnedStr does not invalidate external pointers.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit via compile-time: ffi/pj_str.rs contains no unsafe beyond initial pj_str_t construction.

Source ticket P3-2 specified the PJSIP FFI layer and runtime state, including node N0056 (§47 Memory Ownership & §48 Default Policies) which governs who owns pj_str_t / pj_pool_t memory across the FFI boundary. The memory_ownership_defaults.rs file was created as a stub (`pub struct Model {}` plus the P8-24 marker at line 23) because the ownership model was deferred. This work item implements the memory ownership model and default policies per node N0056.
scope: - src/model/memory_ownership_defaults.rs - replace the stub with the memory ownership model types and default policies
- src/model/mod.rs - re-export the new types
- src/ffi/pj_str.rs - reuse PjOwnedStr (Rust-owned pj_str_t backing) as the concrete ownership primitive
- src/ffi/mod.rs - verify the ownership model integrates with the FFI boundary
- Out of scope: new bindgen bindings, the callback bridge implementation, and any unsafe-code changes in runtime/ (all unsafe remains isolated to ffi/).
- Impact: memory-ownership types available to the FFI layer and runtime state; formalizes who owns callback-parameter memory.
testUnit: UT: [C057] Ownership model classifies PjOwnedStr as Rust-owned; a pj_str_t copied from an FFI callback source is immediately copied to Vec<u8>.
UT: [C057] Default policy marks callback-parameter memory as valid only within callback scope.
UT: [C038] model/memory_ownership_defaults.rs contains no unsafe keyword (grep/compile test).
UT: [C034] Ownership-model helper functions are non-blocking (no allocation in the RT-callback path).
UT: [Normal] Empty-string and >4096-byte inputs satisfy the ownership model invariants.
UT: [Boundary] A pj_str_t with slen=0 and a non-null ptr is classified correctly.
testIntegration: IT: [FFI-boundary] A PjOwnedStr constructed from a callback-provided pj_str_t remains valid after the callback frame is popped (ownership transferred to Rust).
IT: [Module-graph] cargo check succeeds with the new model types re-exported from model/mod.rs.
testExceptions: Real pj_pool_t lifetime semantics require a live PJSUA stack (pjsua-native feature); the ownership model is specified as type-level/documentation invariants and verified with PjOwnedStr unit tests, not against a live pool.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】memory_ownership_defaults.rs defines the ownership model (e.g., an Ownership distinction between Rust-owned and PJSUA-pool-owned, with default policies) and it compiles and re-exports through model/mod.rs.
【Happy path】The default policy matches C057: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory; the original PJSUA ptr is only used as an immediate copy source, never stored.
【Happy path】PjOwnedStr remains the concrete implementation of the Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>) and satisfies the ownership model's Rust-owned policy.
【Error case】The model forbids embedding pj_pool_t-owned memory in Rust structs (type-level/documentation invariant) - no owned pj_pool_t memory in Rust structs.
【Edge case】Empty strings (slen=0) and large inputs (>4096 bytes) remain valid under the ownership model.

Source ticket P3-2 specified AudioWorkerTask with a Tokio JoinHandle for the blocking-pool worker. The handle is stored as `Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` (src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:279) and marked #[allow(dead_code)], so the worker's task lifecycle is not actively managed. This work item replaces the unused Option<JoinHandle> with a non-optional active JoinHandle and integrates shutdown so the handle is always awaited on shutdown.
scope: - src/runtime/audio_worker.rs - change `handle: Option<JoinHandle<()>>` to an active non-optional `JoinHandle<()>`; integrate shutdown to always await it
- src/runtime/mod.rs - verify re-export/compile
- Out of scope: FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort) remains deferred until FFI audio integration is available; AudioMixer behavior unchanged.
- Impact: AudioWorkerTask always owns a live worker task; shutdown deterministically joins the worker.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】After spawn(), the worker holds a non-optional JoinHandle - no Option unwrap needed to observe the running task.
【Happy path】shutdown() sets the shutdown flag and awaits the JoinHandle; after shutdown returns, is_running() == false and the worker task has terminated.
【Happy path】A worker with active sources keeps producing mixed frames until shutdown, then stops cleanly.
【Error case】shutdown() called twice is idempotent - the second call does not panic and returns promptly.
【Edge case】If the worker task panics, shutdown() still resolves (the join returns Err which is logged, not panicked).
【Edge case】spawn() from a tokio runtime context always yields a running JoinHandle (handle.is_finished() == false immediately after spawn).

tickets.title: Migrate to a Debug-friendly sender wrapper and derive Debug for RuntimeCommand

contracts.precondition: Runtime module structure matches RFC §6
contracts.postcondition: runtime/ module compiled and linked
contracts.invariant: Module boundary: runtime/ depends only on tokio + std

contracts.precondition: MPSC channel established between RuntimeHandle and CoreReactor
contracts.postcondition: All commands pass through unbounded MPSC channel in FIFO order
contracts.invariant: Reactor loop processes exactly one command per iteration with no reordering

contracts.precondition: RuntimeHandle is Send + Sync
contracts.postcondition: RuntimeHandle can be shared across tokio tasks and threads safely
contracts.invariant: RuntimeCommand enum and all its fields satisfy Send bounds

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P0-2 specified the RuntimeCommand enum with tokio oneshot reply channels. Because oneshot::Sender is not Debug, Debug was manually implemented (src/runtime/command.rs:148-174) to print only variant names. This work item migrates the reply channel to a Debug-friendly wrapper type so RuntimeCommand can derive Debug and produce richer debug output.
scope: - src/runtime/command.rs - introduce a Debug-friendly sender wrapper (e.g., ReplyChannel<T>), replace `tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<...>` reply fields, and derive/verify Debug on RuntimeCommand
- src/runtime/reactor.rs - update construction/send sites to the wrapper type
- src/runtime/handle.rs - verify submit() sites compile against the wrapper
- Out of scope: changing oneshot reply semantics, FIFO ordering, or Send bounds.
- Impact: RuntimeCommand becomes fully Debug-derivable; debug output can include field summaries instead of just variant names.
testUnit: UT: [C012] RuntimeCommand implements Debug for every variant (compile-time: fn assert_debug<T: Debug>()).
UT: [C011] format!("{:?}", cmd) for a representative variant (Shutdown, AddAudioSource, MakeCall) does not panic and contains the variant name.
UT: [C012] The sender wrapper is Send (compile-time assert).
UT: [C011] Display output unchanged: format!("{}", RuntimeCommand::Shutdown) == "RuntimeCommand::Shutdown".
UT: [Normal] The wrapper round-trips a reply (send through the wrapper, receive on the oneshot) - exactly-once delivery.
UT: [Boundary] Debug output for a variant with a payload field (e.g., MakeCall with account_id) includes the field or a non-sensitive summary.
testIntegration: IT: [Dispatch] Submit a command through RuntimeHandle and receive the reply via the wrapper - identical to before the migration (existing P0-2 tests keep passing).
IT: [Logging] A debug log of a RuntimeCommand in the reactor loop renders without error.
testExceptions: oneshot::Sender itself cannot be made Debug without the wrapper; the migration is the wrapper. Raw sender identity is not exposed in Debug output by design.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】RuntimeCommand derives #[derive(Debug)] (or otherwise produces field-rich debug output) and compiles for every variant, including those carrying a reply channel.
【Happy path】The Debug-friendly sender wrapper implements Debug (e.g., prints "ReplyChannel" or a non-sensitive summary) and is used for all reply fields.
【Happy path】format!("{:?}", RuntimeCommand::Shutdown { reply }) prints the variant and does not panic.

【Happy path】AddAudioSource (which boxes a non-Debug AsyncAudioSource) also produces a working Debug representation (via a scoped manual Debug for that field or a second wrapper), so derivation is total.
【Error case】No behavior change: send_reply()/reactor dispatch still deliver exactly-once results through the wrapper.
【Edge case】The Display impl (format!("{}", cmd)) output is unchanged - it still prints "RuntimeCommand::Variant".
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P0-1 (depends on: P0 defines overall architecture that concurrency model realizes), P2 (depends on: P2 extends RuntimeCommand with M20 variants)
tickets.notes:
- Stub file:line list - src/runtime/command.rs:146.
- Implementation steps: (1) add the ReplyChannel wrapper with a Debug impl; (2) replace reply field types across RuntimeCommand and DispatchCommand; (3) update construction/send sites (reactor.rs, handle.rs, tests); (4) derive Debug on RuntimeCommand (and handle the boxed AsyncAudioSource field); (5) keep Display unchanged; (6) Red tests; (7) Green.
- Dependencies: reactor.rs and handle.rs consume the reply fields; existing P0-2 tests (command.rs:436-730) exercise construction and dispatch - they must be updated to the wrapper and kept green.
- Related tickets: P0-2 (original concurrency model), P2 (extends RuntimeCommand with M20 variants).
tickets.invariants:
- All commands pass through the MPSC channel in FIFO order; the wrapper must not alter dispatch semantics (C011).
- RuntimeCommand and all fields satisfy Send bounds; the wrapper must remain Send (C012).
- runtime/ module boundary is preserved (C010).
tickets.instrumentation: - No new logging required; the richer Debug output benefits existing reactor-loop tracing that formats RuntimeCommand.
tickets.investigation:
- src/runtime/command.rs:146 - the P8-27 stub sits above the manual `impl std::fmt::Debug for RuntimeCommand` (lines 148-174), which matches on variant names and prints only "RuntimeCommand::{Variant}", skipping all fields.
- Line 43 comment: "Debug is manual (not derived) because `Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>` is not Debug." The enum (lines 44-144) has 18 variants; every reply field is `tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<...>>` (not Debug). AddAudioSource (lines 120-123) additionally boxes `dyn AsyncAudioSource` (not Debug). DispatchCommand (lines 217-269) has the same pattern and a manual Debug (lines 392-423).
- What a real implementation must provide: a Debug-friendly wrapper (e.g., `pub(crate) struct ReplyChannel<T>(oneshot::Sender<T>)` with a manual Debug impl), swap all reply fields to the wrapper, handle the non-Debug boxed source (scoped manual Debug for AddAudioSource or a second wrapper), then derive/confirm Debug on RuntimeCommand. send_reply() (lines 426-434) and the reactor must construct the wrapper.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Replace the two near-identical manual match blocks (Debug lines 148-174 and Display lines 177-202) with derive + a single Display helper to avoid drift.
- Add a doc comment on the wrapper explaining why the manual Debug is required (oneshot::Sender not Debug) and that the raw sender is never printed.

tickets.title: Upgrade the Weak<JoinHandle> to Arc and expose it for FFI thread lifecycle inspection once pjsua is linked

contracts.precondition: Rust FFI required to call C PJSUA library functions. Concurrency model defines reactor thread for serialized command execution.
contracts.postcondition: PJSIP FFI layer created with: (1) ffi::bindings module generated by bindgen build.rs with allowlist pattern, (2) PjOwnedStr safe wrapper for pj_str_t with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing, (3) extern C callback functions enqueue NativeEvent, (4) runtime/ modules use only safe SipBackend trait.
contracts.invariant: All unsafe code isolated to ffi/ module. No unsafe keyword in runtime/, client.rs, or config/. Compile-time lint enforces unsafe isolation.

contracts.precondition: Reactor thread owns single source-of-truth ClientState. Tokio runtime provides async RwLock for snapshot sharing.
contracts.postcondition: ClientState with initialized, accounts BTreeMap, calls BTreeMap, transports Vec, capabilities. AccountEntry with id, native_id, config, registration. CallEntry with id, native_id, account_id, state, media. conf_port_id NOT in CallEntry.
contracts.invariant: Read-only snapshots via read().await (never blocking_read()). Updates via write().await (reactor only).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P3-2 (PJSIP FFI Layer, Runtime State & AudioMixer Architecture) specified the reactor-thread concurrency model and the Send+Sync RuntimeHandle, but left the join_handle field as an unused Weak<JoinHandle<()>>. This marker was left as a stub because CoreReactor::spawn returns the JoinHandle separately (reactor.rs:247) and nothing consumes the handle's stored weak reference. This work item resolves it by upgrading the field to Arc<JoinHandle<()>> and exposing a thread-lifecycle inspection accessor on RuntimeHandle for the FFI layer.
scope: - src/runtime/handle.rs:27-29 — replace the #[allow(dead_code)] Weak<JoinHandle<()>> field with Arc<JoinHandle<()>> and add a getter / is_thread_alive() inspection method
- src/runtime/handle.rs:34-44 — update RuntimeHandle::new signature to accept Arc<JoinHandle<()>>
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:63 — pass the spawned thread's join handle into RuntimeHandle::new instead of Weak::new()
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:247 — keep the caller-facing JoinHandle consistent with the Arc stored in the handle
- Out of scope: PJSUA C linkage / bindgen (P8-5); FFI callback registration (P8-21).
- Impact: RuntimeHandle public API; reactor spawn return contract; FFI thread-lifecycle observer can query reactor-thread liveness once PJSIP is linked.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] RuntimeHandle::new with an Arc<JoinHandle> stores the handle and the inspection accessor returns the identical Arc (Arc::ptr_eq).
UT: [Normal] runtime_handle_is_clonable (handle.rs:282) still passes with the Arc-typed field.
UT: [Boundary] inspection reports not-finished for a running reactor thread and finished after the thread is joined.
UT: [Error] construction with a valid Arc never fails; the field is non-optional, so no partial-state path exists.
testIntegration: IT: CoreReactor::spawn returns a RuntimeHandle whose exposed Arc<JoinHandle> refers to the same thread the caller joins; after join(), the handle's inspection method reports finished.
testExceptions: Actual OS-thread mid-life liveness depends on scheduling and cannot be asserted deterministically across platforms; unit tests verify the Arc wiring and thread-id equality, not liveness timings. FFI consumers of the exposed handle require the pjsua-native linkage (P8-5) that is not available in unit tests.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】RuntimeHandle stores the reactor thread's JoinHandle as Arc<JoinHandle<()>> and exposes an inspection accessor (e.g. thread_handle() -> &Arc<JoinHandle<()>> or is_thread_alive()).

【Happy path】CoreReactor::spawn (reactor.rs:56) passes the actual spawned thread's join handle into RuntimeHandle::new, and the stored Arc is the same thread the caller joins at reactor.rs:247 — verified by Arc::ptr_eq or std::thread::Thread::id equality.
【Happy path】RuntimeHandle remains Send + Sync and Clone after the change; the compile-time assert_send/assert_sync tests at handle.rs:272-277 stay green.
【Edge case】A cloned RuntimeHandle shares the same Arc<JoinHandle> — thread inspection from any clone reports the same underlying thread.
【Edge case】The #[allow(dead_code)] on the join_handle field is removed once the Arc is consumed by the inspection accessor.
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P2-4 (depends on: AudioWorkerTask pattern), P3-1 (depends on: configure_codecs via backend), P6 (depends on: state machine transitions update ClientState)
tickets.notes: Stub site: src/runtime/handle.rs:27,29 (field + allow). Order: (1) change the field type to Arc<JoinHandle<()>>; (2) update new() and all call sites; (3) add the inspection accessor; (4) update tests. Callers of RuntimeHandle::new: reactor.rs:63 and the 7 test constructors in handle.rs. Keep the reactor thread std::thread-based per the type assertion at reactor.rs:586. Related: P3-2 (source), P8-5 (bindgen), P8-21 (callback registration).
tickets.invariants: RuntimeHandle remains Send + Sync (Arc<JoinHandle<()>> is Send+Sync because std::thread::JoinHandle<()> is Send+Sync). The reactor thread is still spawned via std::thread (never tokio::task::spawn), so the handle remains a std::thread::JoinHandle — the type assertion at reactor.rs:586 stays green. No unsafe code is introduced in runtime/handle.rs; unsafe remains confined to ffi/ (C038).
tickets.instrumentation: Add tracing::debug! when the reactor thread is observed finished via the exposed handle. Log the thread id/name at spawn so FFI lifecycle logs correlate with the reactor thread.
tickets.investigation: src/runtime/handle.rs:27-29 declares join_handle: Weak<JoinHandle<()>> guarded by #[allow(dead_code)]; the field is written in RuntimeHandle::new (handle.rs:34-44) and never read. src/runtime/reactor.rs:63 constructs the handle with std::sync::Weak::new(), and reactor.rs:247 returns the thread_join JoinHandle to the caller instead — so the stored weak reference can never upgrade (it is always None). The doc comment at handle.rs:15 documents the field under Send + Sync safety as Weak<JoinHandle<()>>. The tests construct handles with Weak::new() at handle.rs:285,296,309,325,349,372,400. A real implementation must change the field type to Arc<JoinHandle<()>>, update new() and all call sites, and add an inspection accessor so the FFI thread-lifecycle observer can query reactor-thread liveness once P8-5/P8-21 land.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the #[allow(dead_code)] once the field is consumed. Update the Send + Sync safety doc comment at handle.rs:15 from Weak<JoinHandle<()>> to Arc<JoinHandle<()>>. Replace the repeated Weak::new() literals in the test module (handle.rs:285,296,309,325,349,372,400) with a shared helper that builds a real Arc so the tests read as prose.
