Source ticket P3-2 specified the dual-client EventBus dispatch (C039) and the NativeEvent to SipEvent conversion pipeline, but left dispatch_event, process_native_event, and extract_event_ids as #[allow(dead_code)] free functions in reactor.rs with no call site. These were left as stubs because the FFI callback bridge (P8-21) that delivers NativeEvents to the reactor is not yet linked, so no event source feeds the loop. This work item resolves them by wiring the three helpers into the reactor loop so NativeEvents arriving from the callback bridge are converted and dispatched.
scope: - src/runtime/reactor.rs:260,294,335 — remove the #[allow(dead_code)] markers and wire dispatch_event / process_native_event / extract_event_ids into the reactor loop
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:80-244 — add a NativeEvent ingestion path (receiver) to the reactor loop and call process_native_event with the backend, client_event_buses, and default_event_bus
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:263-264,297-298 — have the reactor own/create the EventBus instances (currently only parameters, never instantiated in spawn)
- Out of scope: FFI callback-bridge enqueue (P8-21); NativeEvent conversion gaps (P8-20); mock/real backend split (P8-3).
- Impact: production event flow from PJSIP callbacks to SipClient EventBuses; removes the dead-code markers.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] a NativeEvent fed through the wired loop path reaches process_native_event and is published (mirrors process_native_event_call_state_changed_publishes at reactor.rs:526).
UT: [Normal] RegistrationStateChanged with status 200 publishes RegistrationSucceeded (existing test reactor.rs:472 stays green after wiring).
UT: [Error] backend Err publishes RegistrationFailed or Error (existing test reactor.rs:497 stays green).
UT: [Boundary] a P1/P2 event produces no publication (existing test reactor.rs:547 stays green).
UT: [Normal] dispatch_event routing isolation (reactor.rs:377,411,439) stays green.
testIntegration: IT: Spawn the reactor with a MockBackend, inject a NativeEvent through the new ingestion channel, subscribe a default EventBus, and assert the converted SipEvent arrives on the bus.
testExceptions: The real PJSUA callback bridge (P8-21) cannot run without pjsua linkage; integration tests inject NativeEvents directly through the reactor's ingestion channel using MockBackend. EventBus broadcast capacity (2048 at client.rs:100) makes delivery loss-tolerant, so exact-delivery counts are asserted only for single-subscriber control receivers in unit tests.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】The reactor loop receives a NativeEvent (from the callback-bridge channel) and calls process_native_event, which converts it to a SipEvent and routes it through dispatch_event to the correct client/default EventBus.
【Happy path】RegistrationStateChanged events query the backend via get_account_info and publish RegistrationSucceeded / RegistrationFailed / Error (reactor.rs:302-315) — no silent drop.

【Happy path】Non-registration P0 events (CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfDigit) flow through convert_native_event_to_payload plus extract_event_ids and publish with the correct account_id / call_id in EventMeta.
【Error case】Backend errors during event processing are published as SipEventPayload::Error (reactor.rs:306) and never crash the loop.
【Edge case】P1/P2 events (TransportStateChanged, NatDetected, etc.) are dropped without publication, as documented (reactor.rs:316-325).
【Edge case】The reactor owns at least a default_event_bus; client_event_buses maps account_id to the registered SipClient bus so no event is duplicated across clients (C039 invariant).

Order: (1) create a NativeEvent ingestion channel and reactor-owned EventBus instances; (2) call process_native_event in the loop; (3) drop the dead-code markers; (4) add the integration test. Depends on the callback-bridge enqueue shape agreed in P8-21; until PJSIP is linked, tests inject NativeEvent directly. Related: P3-2 (source), P7-2 (dispatch tests), P8-21 (callback bridge), P8-20 (FFI call sites).
tickets.invariants: Single Reactor pattern preserved: all NativeEvents are processed on the one reactor thread and no event is duplicated across clients (C039). The reactor remains the single writer of ClientState (C046). No unsafe code is added to runtime/reactor.rs (C038). EventBus publish remains a loss-tolerant broadcast; the client.rs:100 default capacity (2048) is preserved.
tickets.instrumentation: tracing::info! per published SipEvent (event type, account_id, call_id); tracing::warn! for P1/P2 dropped events and for backend errors that publish Error payloads.
tickets.investigation: reactor.rs:260 marks dispatch_event with #[allow(dead_code)]; the function (262-282) implements account-based routing but is never called. process_native_event (295-327) implements the registration flow and the generic conversion but is also dead. extract_event_ids (336-355) is called only from process_native_event, so it too is dead. The reactor loop in spawn (80-244) handles only DispatchCommand variants; there is no NativeEvent receiver and no EventBus instance owned by the reactor — client.rs:100 creates an EventBus on the SipClient side but nothing connects it to dispatch_event. A real implementation must add a NativeEvent channel (the callback bridge's enqueue target, P8-21), have the reactor own a default_event_bus and a client_event_buses map, and call process_native_event from the loop for each received event, preserving the C039 no-duplication invariant.

Extract the repeated catch_unwind / panic-payload block (reactor.rs:85-114,153-183,185-222) into a helper so the loop reads as prose. Replace the trailing let _ = native_id; at reactor.rs:199 with a structured use or an explicit rename.

Source ticket P3-2 specified the call-state mapping where CallDirection (Outgoing/Incoming) discriminates CONNECTING into Trying vs Ringing, but left CallDirection and convert_call_state_with_previous with #[allow(dead_code)] and the on_incoming_call FFI callback (ffi/callback.rs:31) as a no-op that never records a direction. These were left as stubs because the FFI callback bridge (P8-21) that would deliver the incoming-call direction is not yet linked. This work item resolves them by wiring CallDirection into the on_incoming_call callback and calling convert_call_state_with_previous from Reactor call processing to discriminate Trying vs Ringing.
scope: - src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:47-53 — remove #[allow(dead_code)] from CallDirection and consume it in the reactor path
- src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:112-125 — remove #[allow(dead_code)], use the call_id parameter (drop the _ prefix), and make convert_call_state_with_previous the CONNECTING path
- src/ffi/callback.rs:31-37 — on_incoming_call must record the incoming call (enqueue a NativeEvent carrying the Incoming direction) instead of dropping its arguments
- src/runtime/reactor.rs — the reactor call-state processing must call convert_call_state_with_previous with the resolved CallDirection
- Out of scope: full callback registration via pjsua_config.cb (P8-21); bindgen bindings (P8-5).
- Impact: CONNECTING inbound calls now emit OutgoingCallRinging instead of always OutgoingCallTrying.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] convert_call_state_with_previous(CONNECTING, Incoming) returns OutgoingCallRinging (existing test at m20_callstate_mapping.rs:192 stays green).
UT: [Normal] convert_call_state_with_previous(CONNECTING, Outgoing) returns OutgoingCallTrying (existing test at :180 stays green).
UT: [Normal] on_incoming_call records an incoming call / enqueues a NativeEvent with direction Incoming.

UT: [Error] a call state with no resolvable direction falls back to convert_call_state's default (Trying).

testExceptions: The on_incoming_call FFI callback cannot be invoked from a unit test without a live PJSUA stack (pjsua-native feature, P8-5/P8-21); unit tests cover the direction-recording helper and the conversion function directly, and integration tests inject the NativeEvent.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】An incoming call at CONNECTING with CallDirection::Incoming produces SipEventPayload::OutgoingCallRinging via convert_call_state_with_previous.
【Happy path】An outgoing call at CONNECTING with CallDirection::Outgoing produces OutgoingCallTrying (unchanged behavior).
【Happy path】on_incoming_call (ffi/callback.rs:31) no longer drops its arguments — it records the incoming call so the reactor can resolve CallDirection::Incoming.
【Edge case】Non-CONNECTING states delegate to convert_call_state unchanged (m20_callstate_mapping.rs:123).
【Edge case】The #[allow(dead_code)] markers on CallDirection (line 48) and convert_call_state_with_previous (line 112) are removed once consumed.

tickets.title: Implement PhaseTimeout handling for per-call timeout tracking during shutdown

contracts.precondition: SipClient has been initialized (initialize() completed successfully); reactor is running and accepting commands
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownSpec orchestrates idempotent shutdown: (1) atomic is_shutdown_started swap prevents re-entry, (2) all active calls are BYE/CANCELed, (3) accounts unregistered, (4) audio worker drained, (5) backend.shutdown() called, (6) reactor loop exits
contracts.invariant: Shutdown is idempotent: first call executes full sequence and returns Ok(()); second and subsequent calls return Ok(()) immediately without executing the sequence again

contracts.precondition: ShutdownSpec.is_shutdown_started() returns true after first atomic swap
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownCommandRouter.classify() correctly routes commands during shutdown: GetAccountInfo → Permit, ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect → Reject(InvalidState), all others → Reject(InvalidState). Reactor applies this routing before command execution.
contracts.invariant: GetAccountInfo is always Permitted during shutdown (read-only state check). ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are always Rejected during shutdown (media mutation is unsafe during teardown).

Source ticket P4-3 (Shutdown, Media Bridge, HTTP/WS Protocol & SQLite Schema) specified ShutdownSpec as an idempotent phase-ordered shutdown orchestrator with a per-phase timeout, but the timeout field is stored in the struct (shutdown_specification.rs:144-146) and never read, and ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout (lines 87-90) is never constructed. This marker was left as a stub because CancelCalls iterates calls with no deadline and no per-call timeout accounting. This work item resolves it by implementing PhaseTimeout handling for per-call timeout tracking during shutdown.
scope: - src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:144-146 — remove #[allow(dead_code)] and consume the timeout field
- src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:217-261 — execute_phase (especially CancelCalls) applies the per-phase timeout; a phase that exceeds it produces ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout
- src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:232-239 — per-call hangup deadline tracking (deadline per call and an overall phase deadline)
- src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:87-90 — ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout becomes reachable
- Out of scope: ShutdownCommandRouter command gating (P4-3/C045); audio drain coordination (P4-3/C050).
- Impact: shutdown CancelCalls no longer hangs indefinitely on a stuck backend; timeout errors are observable.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] a phase that completes within the timeout returns Ok (existing shutdown_sequence_executes_idempotently at shutdown_specification.rs:332 stays green).
UT: [Error] a backend hangup that blocks beyond the timeout yields ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout with the correct phase and timeout.
UT: [Boundary] timeout=Duration::ZERO with a non-completing phase returns PhaseTimeout without panic.
UT: [Boundary] the sequence continues after a PhaseTimeout and returns the first error (C044 continue-on-error).
testIntegration: IT: Drive ShutdownSpec with a MockBackend whose hangup blocks (or a timing-aware backend), and assert execute_sequence returns PhaseTimeout while is_shutdown_started() stays true and the remaining phases still run.
testExceptions: Deterministic wall-clock timing cannot be asserted in unit tests without sleeping; tests use a timeout-aware backend (or a MockBackend configured to report hangup as pending) and assert the PhaseTimeout error type and the continuation behavior rather than exact durations. tokio::time::timeout keeps the async tests fast.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】A phase that completes within the configured timeout returns Ok and records no timeout (existing shutdown tests stay green).

【Error case】A phase (e.g. CancelCalls) that exceeds the configured timeout produces ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout { phase, timeout } — and, per C044, subsequent phases still execute and the first error is returned.
【Edge case】The timeout is applied per phase boundary (per-call deadline plus an overall phase deadline), not as an unbounded per-call wait.
【Edge case】A zero or very small timeout does not panic — it degrades to an immediate PhaseTimeout for slow backends.

tickets.title: Event System Core — EventBus, NativeEvent Conversion, Dual Client Routing

contracts.precondition: Event model established — SipEventPayload enum with all P0 variants (RegistrationStarted, CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfDigit), SipEvent wrapper with EventMeta, and AccountId newtype exist (N0018). Input schema: EventBus::new(control_capacity: usize, raw_sip_capacity: Option<usize>) -> Self. publish(event: SipEvent) called from Reactor context.
contracts.postcondition: EventBus struct with control: broadcast::Sender<SipEvent> and raw_sip: Option<broadcast::Sender<RawSipMessage>> fields. Methods: new(), subscribe_control() -> Receiver<SipEvent>, subscribe_raw_sip() -> Option<Receiver<RawSipMessage>>, publish(SipEvent), publish_raw_sip(RawSipMessage). AccountEventReceiver with account_id filtering loop that drops non-matching events. Output assertion: publish() delivers to all subscribers; Lagged(n) detectable.
contracts.invariant: AccountEventReceiver::recv() loops across broadcast recv() calls, filtering only SipEvent where event.meta.account_id == Some(self.account_id). Non-matching events are silently dropped. recv() is async (not busy-loop). Verify via test: publish event for account A with receiver for account B — event is skipped.

contracts.precondition: Event model defined — SipEventPayload enum with separation of control events vs RawSIP messages. Control channel capacity defined (default 2048). RawSIP channel is optional (None when disabled).
contracts.postcondition: Design rationale: control bus for registration/call/DTMF/ICE/transport/client-lifecycle/error events; raw_sip bus for raw SIP messages. Delivery: lossy via broadcast channel, no retransmission, Lagged(n) detection. Source of truth is query API (accounts(), call_state()), not events. Verify via: test with slow consumer verifies Lagged(n) is returned.
contracts.invariant: Events are observation-only, not source of truth. Query APIs (SipClient::accounts(), call_state()) are the authoritative state. Event loss does not corrupt client state — lost events can be recovered by re-querying state. Assert via: test that drops all events then calls query API — state is consistent.

contracts.precondition: Event model defined — SipEventPayload enum with all variants, NativeEvent enum with P0/P1/P2 variants, CallState/CallMediaState enums defined, RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo variant exists for RegistrationStateChanged flow.
contracts.postcondition: Complete NativeEvent-to-SipEventPayload mapping: RegistrationStarted->RegistrationStarted, CallStateChanged->OutgoingCallStarted/CallConnected/CallDisconnected/etc. via convert_call_state(), CallMediaStateChanged->MediaActive/CallHeld/MediaError via convert_call_media_state(), DtmfDigit->DtmfReceived, RegistrationStateChanged issues GetAccountInfo command then publishes RegistrationSucceeded/Failed. Output assertion: convert_native_event_to_payload(event, backend) -> Option<SipEventPayload> covers all NativeEvent variants.
contracts.invariant: All NativeEvent variants are handled — P0 variants produce Some(SipEventPayload), P1/P2 variants (TransportStateChanged, IceTransportError, CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected) return None with documented rationale. Exhaustive match on NativeEvent in conversion function. Verify via test: match each NativeEvent variant and assert expected output type.

contracts.precondition: NativeEvent-to-SipEventPayload mapping complete — CallState struct defined with discriminants matching pjsip_inv_state values. CallEntry with previous_state field for CONNECTING discrimination.
contracts.postcondition: All 5 pjsip_inv_state values (0-4) mapped to CallState: NULL->None, CALLING->Calling, CONNECTING->Trying/Ringing (discriminated), CONFIRMED->Active, DISCONNECTED->Disconnecting. CallMediaState mapped: NONE->None, ACTIVE->MediaActive, LOCAL_HOLD->CallHeld, REMOTE_HOLD->CallHeld, ERROR->MediaError. Output assertion: convert_call_state(call_id, state) -> Option<SipEventPayload> and convert_call_media_state(call_id) -> Option<SipEventPayload>.
contracts.invariant: pjsip_inv_state values 0-4 covered without wildcard match — match arm for each discriminant. CONNECTING discrimination: use previous call state (Calling vs Incoming) from CallEntry. Safety fallback to Trying when previous state unknown.

contracts.precondition: NativeEvent-to-SipEventPayload mapping complete — RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo defined with native_acc_id: pjsua_acc_id and reply_tx: oneshot::Sender<Result<AccountInfoSnapshot, SipError>>. AccountInfoSnapshot struct defined.
contracts.postcondition: RegistrationStateChanged flow: NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged triggers RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo -> backend.get_account_info() -> AccountInfoSnapshot. Status 200 -> RegistrationSucceeded, 4xx/5xx/6xx -> RegistrationFailed. Both paths publish a SipEvent on EventBus. Output assertion: RegistrationStateChanged always results in a published event.
contracts.invariant: MockBackend testable — MockBackend::get_account_info() returns controllable AccountInfoSnapshot. RegistrationStateChanged handler is tested with mock backend without requiring live PJSIP. Verify: inject RegistrationStateChanged, mock returns status 200 -> verify RegistrationSucceeded published.

contracts.precondition: DTMF spec defined — DtmfReceivedInfo struct, DtmfMethod enum, send_dtmf returns RpcResult<()>. DtmfSentInfo struct defined with method: DtmfMethod, digit: char, status: Result<(), SentDtmfError>, pjsip_status: Option<pj_status_t>. SentDtmfError enum: PjsipError(pj_status_t), Timeout.
contracts.postcondition: DtmfSentInfo two-phase design: send_dtmf() synchronous return Ok(()) means command accepted by reactor. Async DtmfSent event published either via PJSIP callback (preferred) or 500ms timeout fallback. DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms configurable via ClientConfig (default 500ms). Output assertion: DtmfSent is always published eventually.
contracts.invariant: 500ms timeout fallback when PJSIP callback unavailable — verified via test with tokio::time::pause() that advances time 500ms and checks DtmfSent with Status::Err(Timeout) is published. Timeout value configurable via DtmfConfig.

contracts.precondition: FFI layer and SipBackend exist — PjsuaBackend singleton (OnceLock), Reactor with command queue. SipClient instances registered with different account_ids.
contracts.postcondition: Single Reactor + EventBus split: global_runtime() unchanged, single Reactor maintained. client_event_buses: HashMap<AccountId, EventBus> for per-client dispatch. account_id=None events published to all client buses. account_id=Some(aid) events published only to matching client bus. Unmatched account_id -> default_event_bus.
contracts.invariant: Single Reactor + EventBus split maintained — no second Reactor created. Client EventBuses are separate broadcast::Sender instances sharing no channel state beyond their respective capacity. Verify via: two clients registered with different accounts, event for account A not visible on account B's bus.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

This ticket implements the complete event system: EventBus with control/raw_sip broadcast channels (N0019), design decisions for loss-tolerant delivery with Lagged detection (N0020), NativeEvent to SipEventPayload conversion for all P0/P1/P2 priority events (N0021), CallState/CallMediaState mapping from pjsip_inv_state and media_status (N0022), RegistrationStateChanged via RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo pattern (N0023), DtmfSent two-phase design with timeout fallback (N0029), and Dual Client PJSIP callback routing with account_id-based EventBus dispatch (N0038).

## Goal
The P0-5 event system provides the complete bridge between PJSIP C callbacks and Rust async event consumers. It defines the SipEventPayload enum (all P0 variants: Registration/Call/DTMF; P1: Transport/ICE; P2: supplemental), the EventBus with split control/raw_sip broadcast channels, the NativeEvent-to-SipEventPayload conversion functions, and the Dual Client routing infrastructure. Every PJSIP callback-generated event is delivered to the correct SipClient's EventBus as a typed SipEvent struct.

## Purpose
SipClient consumers (UI layer, audio pipeline, logging) need observable, structured notifications about SIP state changes. Without this event system, application code would need to poll for state or interpret raw PJSIP callbacks directly. The EventBus provides a decoupled publish-subscribe pattern where:
- Reactor publishes SipEvents onto broadcast channels
- Multiple consumers independently subscribe and filter (via AccountEventReceiver)
- RawSIP messages are isolated on a separate bus to prevent control event loss

This is the primary async communication channel between the synchronous PJSIP thread (C callbacks) and the async Rust world (tokio tasks).

## Motivation
This is the foundational event infrastructure for the entire crate. All observable SIP behavior — registration status changes, call state transitions, DTMF events, media state changes — flows through this system. Every downstream feature (P2-2 error payloads, P2-4 audio pipeline, P4-1 registration state machine) depends on events being delivered. The current stub (src/client.rs uses mpsc::Receiver<()>) blocks all downstream development.

Without this ticket:
- No SipEventPayload type exists (all stubs)
- NativeEvent conversion is unimplemented
- SipClient returns dummy event receiver (cannot observe any SIP events)
- Dual Client mode (multiple SipClient instances) has no event routing

## Constraints
- Broadcast channel (lossy delivery): tokio::sync::broadcast is the only supported channel type. No reliable delivery, no per-subscriber retransmission. This is by design (N0020).
- PJSUA dependency: NativeEvent types mirror PJSIP callback signatures (pjsip_inv_state, pjsua_call_media_status). Any PJSIP version mismatch may require updating the mapping.
- Single Reactor constraint: global_runtime() must remain unchanged. Dual Client uses EventBus dispatch only — no second Reactor.
- All implementation targets are stub files (pub enum State {} / pub trait Service {}). This is net-new implementation, not refactoring of existing code.
- DtmfSent 500ms timeout: This is a fallback for when PJSIP does not fire a send-complete callback. The timeout may race with actual PJSIP callback delivery (firing both DtmfSent events) — consumer must handle duplicates.

### Goal (P7-2 re-implementation)
Close all five ABC inspection gaps in the P0-5 event system: (O-001) make RegistrationStateChanged actually publish RegistrationSucceeded/RegistrationFailed via the RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo → MockBackend::get_account_info() → registration_status_to_payload flow on the client EventBus; (O-002) implement the DtmfSent 500ms timeout fallback (spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout + DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms) with a tokio::time::pause() test; (O-003) implement production Reactor dispatch_event()/client_event_buses/default_event_bus and test the production code; (O-004) add SipClient::accounts()/call_state() authoritative query methods and prove events are observation-only; (O-005) assert the exact Lagged(n) count.
### Purpose (P7-2 re-implementation)
The prior implementation produced green tests that did not exercise the production publication/dispatch flows: RegistrationStateChanged never published an event, DtmfSent never fired as a timeout, dual-client routing existed only inside test bodies, the query API did not exist, and Lagged(n) was asserted loosely. The re-implementation makes every contract (C020-C024, C030, C039) verifiable against production code so a violation fails a test assertion.
### Motivation (P7-2 re-implementation)
The ABC Inspection Pipeline confirmed that the contracts' preconditions/postconditions/invariants were not translated into tests of production behavior — Evaluation A/B/C all failed for O-001..O-003. Downstream tickets (P2-2 error payloads, P2-4 audio pipeline, P4-1 registration state machine, P0-6 FFI bridge) depend on these events actually being delivered. Leaving the gaps means contract violations are undetectable, so the re-implementation must ship production code + tests together.
### Constraints (P7-2 re-implementation)
- Single Reactor constraint: global_runtime() unchanged — dual-client dispatch is EventBus-only (C039).
- DtmfSent timeout may race with the real PJSIP callback; consumers must tolerate duplicate DtmfSent events (N0029).
- tokio::time::pause() requires the `test-util` tokio feature — a Cargo.toml feature addition is mandatory for the O-002 deterministic timeout test (no runtime dependency change).
- No new crates; the production flow must be testable with MockBackend (no live PJSIP).
- CallMediaStateChanged currently hardcodes media_status=1 ([::STUB::] P4-2) — P7-2 keeps this stub but must not regress it.

**Scope of changes (P7-2 re-implementation — ABC closure):**
  - [Path] New production code: src/runtime/reactor.rs (add process_native_event + dispatch_event + client_event_buses: HashMap<AccountId, EventBus> + default_event_bus), src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs (add spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout), src/config.rs (add DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms + dtmf field on ClientConfig), src/client.rs (add accounts()/call_state() query methods). Test/verification: src/runtime/backend.rs (unit-test MockBackend::get_account_info), src/api/eventbus_receiver.rs (exact Lagged(n) count + production dispatch tests + fix the same-AccountId-key test bug), Cargo.toml (add tokio `test-util` feature).
  - [Action] Add: Reactor::process_native_event(NativeEvent) — issues GetAccountInfo for RegistrationStateChanged and publishes RegistrationSucceeded/RegistrationFailed on the client EventBus; Reactor::dispatch_event(SipEvent) — Some(account_id)→matching client_event_buses entry, unmatched→default_event_bus, None→all buses; spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout(call_id, method, digit, timeout_ms) publishing DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)}; DtmfConfig { sent_timeout_ms: u64 } with Default=500; SipClient::accounts() and SipClient::call_state(). Modify: ClientConfig (add dtmf field), Reactor fields. Test-only: tokio `test-util` feature.
  - [Detail] ABC O-001: src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs:88 returns None for RegistrationStateChanged and registration_status_to_payload (src/state/m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs:50) has no production call site — the Reactor must perform the GetAccountInfo flow and publish. ABC O-002: no DtmfSent timeout production code exists (only DtmfSentInfo struct + DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS const) — add spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout + DtmfConfig. ABC O-003: no dispatch_event/client_event_buses/default_event_bus in the Reactor — add production routing and test it. ABC O-004: SipClient lacks accounts()/call_state() — add authoritative query methods. ABC O-005: eventbus_lagged_detection asserts Lagged(_) — tighten to Lagged(2).
  - [Before → After] Before: NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged → None (no event ever published); DtmfSent timeout never fires; dual-client routing only simulated inline in tests; SipClient has no query API; Lagged count unasserted. After: RegistrationStateChanged → GetAccountInfo → RegistrationSucceeded/Failed published on the client EventBus (exactly one per reply); DtmfSent published via spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout (default 500ms) with Err(Timeout); Reactor::dispatch_event routes by account_id with default fallback; SipClient::accounts()/call_state() authoritative; eventbus_lagged_detection asserts Lagged(2).
  - [API] New public methods: SipClient::accounts() -> Result<Vec<AccountSnapshot>, SipError>, SipClient::call_state() -> Result<Vec<CallSnapshot>, SipError>. New public type: DtmfConfig { sent_timeout_ms: u64 } (+ builder setter dtmf_sent_timeout_ms on ClientConfigBuilder). Reactor additions are pub(crate): process_native_event, dispatch_event, client_event_buses, default_event_bus. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout is pub(crate) in src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs.
  - [Schema] No data persistence changes.
  - [Config] ClientConfig gains `dtmf: DtmfConfig` field (serde default = 500ms) — backward compatible for JSON configs. Cargo.toml tokio features += "test-util" (dev-time only).
  - [Dep] No new crates. tokio `test-util` feature added (test-time only, no runtime dependency change).

**Out of scope (P7-2 re-implementation):**
  - [Excluded item] PJSIP FFI callback bridge (P0-6) — NativeEvent generation from real PJSIP callbacks.
  - [Why excluded] The FFI bridge is P0-6's ticket; P7-2 provides the conversion + publication flow driven by MockBackend-injected NativeEvents.
  - [Excluded item] Real PjsuaBackend::get_account_info() (P0-6/P4-2) — MockBackend is the test double.
  - [Why excluded] pjsua_acc_get_info() requires a live pjsua instance; deferred.
  - [Excluded item] P1/P2 NativeEvent conversions (Transport/ICE, CallTsx, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected).
  - [Why excluded] Only P0 events in this round; P1/P2 return None with documented rationale (N0021).
  - [Excluded item] Sequence number for event-audio correlation.
  - [Why excluded] Separate future ticket.
  - [Excluded item] RawSIP message parsing.
  - [Why excluded] Only the raw_sip channel + RawSipMessage type are defined; parsing deferred.
  - [Excluded item] Full DtmfSent callback-vs-timeout race deduplication.
  - [Why excluded] Consumers must handle duplicates by design (N0029); dedup is a consumer concern.

**Affected areas (P7-2 re-implementation):**
  - [Component] SipClient (src/client.rs) — gains accounts()/call_state() query methods; existing events: EventBus field unchanged.
  - [Nature] API surface addition (non-breaking): new query methods; ClientConfig gains dtmf field with serde default.
  - [Response] Existing consumers: no breaking change; new methods additive.
  - [Component] Reactor (src/runtime/reactor.rs) — command loop gains process_native_event publication + dispatch_event routing.
  - [Nature] Runtime behavior: RegistrationStateChanged now publishes events (was silent); DtmfSent timeout now publishes events (was silent).
  - [Response] Consumers observing these flows gain new notifications — verify no consumer depends on their absence (C024/C030 mandate the publication).
  - [Component] src/api/eventbus_receiver.rs + src/runtime/backend.rs tests — dual-client routing tests must target production dispatch_event, not inline re-implementations; MockBackend::get_account_info gets unit tests.
  - [Nature] Test precision (ABC C criteria) + contract translation (ABC A criteria).
  - [Response] Rewrite the buggy dual_client_dispatch_routes_to_correct_bus test (both buses under same AccountId key); add production dispatch tests.

testExceptions: Exception: NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged actual pjsua_acc_get_info() FFI call cannot be tested in unit environment — it requires a live pjsua library initialized with accounts. Reason: pjsua_acc_get_info() is a C FFI function that requires a running pjsua instance with registered accounts (not testable in pure Rust unit context). This is not an architectural defect — the MockBackend::get_account_info() alternative provides the same data shape for unit testing, and the real FFI call is covered by integration tests (P0-6+). Alternative: MockBackend::get_account_info() validates conversion logic without FFI.

Exception: Actual PJSIP callback invocation (on_reg_state2, on_call_state, on_dtmf_digit) cannot be unit-tested — these are C→Rust callbacks triggered by a live PJSIP stack. Reason: FFI callback registration and invocation (not testable without PjsuaBackend from P0-6). This is not an architectural defect — MockBackend simulated NativeEvent injection covers the conversion logic, and integration tests with PjsuaBackend (P0-6+) cover the full callback path. Alternative: MockBackend supplies NativeEvent directly for conversion tests.

Exception: Real-time DTMF timing variance cannot be precisely tested — actual PJSIP callback vs timeout race depends on system scheduling. Reason: The 500ms timeout is a wall-clock timer; actual PJSIP callback may arrive just before or after (not testable deterministically). This is not an architectural defect — tokio::time::pause() provides deterministic simulation for unit tests, and production behavior is verified by integration tests with real PJSIP. Alternative: tokio::time::pause() simulates deterministic timing.

Exception: Dual Client concurrency race condition (simultaneous NativeEvent arrives during client registration/deregistration) — not testable automatically without complex concurrency harness. Reason: Client registration/deregistration is a rare operation; race window is theoretically present but practically zero (not testable in automated unit environment). This is not an architectural defect — the dispatch function is deterministic, and registration/deregistration is serialized through the reactor command queue, eliminating the race in practice. Alternative: Manual stress test in QA phase; unit dispatch tests cover deterministic routing logic.

Exception: RegistrationStateChanged pjsua_acc_get_info() returning a timeout/error status from a live PJSIP stack cannot be simulated in a unit test. Reason: A live registration timeout depends on the SIP registrar's actual non-response, which requires a real network peer and is not testable in a deterministic unit environment. This is not an architectural defect — MockBackend::get_account_info() can be configured to return Err or any status code, exercising the production failure publication path deterministically. Alternative: MockBackend returns Err(ReactorError::BackendError) and the test asserts RegistrationFailed/Error is published on the EventBus.

[Happy path] A single SipClient is initialized, registers a SIP account, makes a call, and receives the call state transition events (OutgoingCallStarted -> OutgoingCallTrying -> CallConnected) on the AccountEventReceiver subscribed to that account_id. Each event has correct EventMeta (timestamp, event_id, account_id, call_id).

[Error case] A NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged fires for an account where pjsua_acc_get_info() fails (returns error). The EventBus delivers a RegistrationFailed event containing the SipError with details. The client is not left in an indeterminate state — the query API returns the correct registration state.

[Edge case] Two SipClient instances share the same PjsuaBackend (Dual Client mode). An incoming call event for account_id=A is published. Client A's AccountEventReceiver receives CallStateChanged; Client B's AccountEventReceiver (subscribed to account_id=B) must NOT receive the event. account_id=None lifecycle events (ClientInitialized, ClientShutdown) must be received by both clients.

[Error case] RegistrationStateChanged with backend.get_account_info() returning Err(ReactorError::BackendError): the production flow publishes exactly one failure SipEvent (RegistrationFailed or Error) — no silent drop; then SipClient::accounts()/call_state() still returns authoritative state consistent with the mock (O-001 + O-004, C021 + C024). Dual-client dispatch with an unmatched account_id falls back to default_event_bus — no panic, no misrouting (O-003).

[Edge case] Dual Client production dispatch: two SipClient instances with account_ids A and B registered in client_event_buses; dispatch_event(event for A) → client A's bus receives it and client B's bus does not (TryRecvError::Empty) — proving the C039 isolation invariant against production code, not a test-local HashMap. account_id=None lifecycle events reach both buses plus default_event_bus. tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] EventBus::publish() must never block — broadcast::Sender::send() is non-blocking by design. SipEventPayload must be Clone + Debug. EventBus must be Clone (all clones share same Sender). NativeEvent conversion must be total over defined P0 variants.
- [Error invariant] On Lagged(n), the receiver skips n messages and resumes from current position — no crash or state corruption. AccountEventReceiver must not panic on Lagged(n). DtmfSent timeout must not abort ongoing operations.
- [Internal state invariant] EventBus Sender is shared across all Clones. AccountEventReceiver holds its own broadcast Receiver. Reactor owns the EventBus Sender + client_event_buses map. client_event_buses is only mutated by SipClient initialization/shutdown, not by event dispatch.
- [Boundary invariant] EventBus default capacity 2048 must accommodate ~100 concurrent calls (~20 events/call). RawSIP channel capacity must be configured independently. DtmfSent timeout default 500ms must be less than typical PJSIP DTMF duration.
- [Normal condition] Reactor::dispatch_event() must route each event to exactly one destination: Some(account_id) matching a client_event_buses key → that bus only; Some(account_id) matching no key → default_event_bus; None (lifecycle) → default_event_bus + every registered client bus (C039). RegistrationStateChanged must publish exactly one RegistrationSucceeded/RegistrationFailed event per GetAccountInfo reply on both success and error paths (C024).
- [Error invariant] RegistrationStateChanged with backend.get_account_info() returning Err must still publish a failure event on the EventBus — no silent drop, no reactor state corruption (C024). DtmfSent timeout fallback must not abort any ongoing call operation — it only publishes DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)} (C030).
- [Internal state invariant] client_event_buses is owned by the Reactor and only mutated during SipClient initialization/shutdown (serialized via the reactor command queue) — dispatch_event() never observes a half-mutated map. DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms is read once at SendDtmf dispatch time; later config changes do not affect already-queued timers (C030). SipClient::accounts()/call_state() read the authoritative ClientState, not the event stream (C021).
- [Boundary invariant] Lagged(n) count equals the number of skipped messages (broadcast channel semantics) — asserted exactly, not matched with a wildcard (C020). EventBus default capacity 2048 must accommodate ~100 concurrent calls (~20 events/call); DtmfSent timeout default 500ms must be less than typical PJSIP DTMF duration; sent_timeout_ms is configurable via DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms (C030).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

## Goal
Define and implement the siprs-server crate specification: standalone server mode (ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode), HTTP/WS protocol layer (18 REST endpoints + 2 WebSocket paths + AudioFrameHeader binary protocol), SQLite persistence schema (4 tables via SeaORM + rusqlite bundled), semver/networking reference information (versioning policy, TLS cert info, DNS delegation), and lib.rs module/export declarations — all as specified by RFC nodes N0057, N0058, N0061, N0062, N0064, N0066, N0067.

## Purpose
This ticket transforms the RFC design for the server crate into concrete implementation artifacts: the config structs and protocol data structures that form the foundation of siprs-server. These types are the layer-5 (API layer) building blocks that downstream tickets (P4-3 route handlers, P4-4 WS handlers, P4-5 SQLite DAO) depend on. Without this ticket, no server-mode code can compile.

## Motivation
The siprs crate core (layer 1-4) is fully specified and partially implemented (P0/P1/P2-2 accomplished). The server mode is the next architectural layer needed for the zasso ecosystem to provide a network-accessible SIP API. Multiple downstream tickets (P4-series) are blocked on these type definitions. Additionally, the current source tree has `[::STUB::]` markers in sqlite_schema.rs and semver_sip_networking.rs that must be resolved.

## Constraints
- Crate uses rusqlite bundled feature (no system SQLite dependency). This must be reflected in Cargo.toml.
- SeaORM migration management must follow the Makefile convention from mycute project.
- AudioFrameHeader must use repr(C,packed) for ABI stability across Rust version upgrades (current size discovered: 30 bytes, not 24 as originally specified — spec correction needed).
- AuthMode enum has exactly 3 variants (LocalhostOnly, ApiKey, Jwt) — variant count invariant enforced by test.
- ServerConfig must at minimum derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize for config file loading.
- DEFAULT_SIPRS_PORT = 3910 — must match the zasso ecosystem port convention (RT_PORT = 3910).

### Goal

### Goal
Close all 8 ABC Inspection gaps in the P2-3 standalone-server implementation: (O-001) add a spec-verification test reading specs/P7-3.md asserting the 4 implementation target files; (O-002) test DatabasePool::open() invalid-path Err and init_schema()/query_tables() 4-table creation; (O-003) pin all 20 path constants to exact RFC S54 values; (O-004) test SequenceGenerator::next() over 1M iterations for monotonicity and uniqueness; (O-005) assert exact ConfigError variants (LocalhostRequiresLoopback, JwtRequiresSecret) instead of message substrings; (O-006) pin CREATE TABLE column types (username TEXT NOT NULL, password BLOB NOT NULL, domain TEXT NOT NULL); (O-007) assert CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased section and CARGO_PKG_VERSION starts with "0."; (O-008) add an external integration test referencing siprs::{ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode} at crate root.

### Purpose
The prior implementation produced green tests that did not pin the exact wire/config contracts: path constants were only checked non-empty/unique, error kinds were asserted by message substring, DatabasePool's init_schema()/query_tables() were never exercised, SequenceGenerator monotonicity was tested with a hand-built Vec instead of 1M generator iterations, and no test verified the spec file or crate-root re-exports. The re-implementation makes every contract (C058, C059, C062, C063, C064, C065, C067, C068) verifiable against production code and the P7-3 spec so a violation fails a test assertion.

### Motivation
The ABC Inspection Pipeline confirmed the contracts' preconditions/postconditions/invariants were not translated into precise tests — Evaluation A/C failed for O-001..O-008. Downstream tickets (P4-3 route handlers, P4-4 WS handlers, P4-5 SQLite DAO) depend on these type definitions being correct and provable. Leaving the gaps means contract violations are undetectable, so the re-implementation must ship production types + precise tests together.

1. Add SQLite dependencies (rusqlite bundled, sea-orm sqlite) to Cargo.toml
2. Implement src/model/sqlite_schema.rs with SeaORM entities for 4 tables
3. Implement src/config/semver_sip_networking.rs with versioning policy constants and TLS info types
4. Add safe AudioFrameHeader::to_bytes() and ::from_bytes() methods in http_ws_protocol.rs
5. Expand test coverage in all affected files — match testUnit spec exactly
6. Fix lying comments in http_ws_protocol.rs tests (24-byte comment → 30-byte)
7. Verify re-exports in lib.rs and config.rs
8. Update CHANGELOG.md unreleased section

## Risks:
- AudioFrameHeader size discrepancy (RFC says 24, actual 30) could cause wire incompatibility if other implementations match RFC literally. Must document this clearly.
- sea-orm with sqlite may add significant compile time. Consider Feature flag gating SQLite-heavy features behind a `sqlite-storage` feature.
- The event_id vs seq field ambiguity in EventMeta/SipEvent could cause confusion in sequence number usage between P2-3 and P4-4.

## Caveats:
- The 30-byte AudioFrameHeader is the actual compiled size (verified by existing tests). The RFC documentation should be updated to match.
- rusqlite bundled feature statically links SQLite — increases binary size by ~1MB but eliminates system dependency.
- Makefile migration commands (gen-migration, migrate-up, etc.) are defined at the workspace level, not in this crate.

## Open items:
- Whether to declare `pub mod model;` in lib.rs or keep model as a private implementation module. Decision: make it private until the crate split (B1 boundary).
- Whether SeaORM migrations should live in siprs or siprs-server crate. Decision: migrations live with sqlite_schema.rs in siprs (types), executed in siprs-server.

## Future improvements:
- After crate split (B1), siprs-core removes SQLite dependency entirely; siprs-server owns the database layer.
- After 1.0 release, add cargo semver-checks CI step per C067 invariant.
- Consider zerocopy crate for safe AudioFrameHeader byte reinterpretation instead of manual to_bytes/from_bytes.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Boy Scout Rule — translatability improvements for P2-3:

    1. FIX MISLEADING COMMENTS IN http_ws_protocol.rs:
       - Line 63: "NOTE: The RFC specifies 24 bytes..." is correct as-is, but test comments on lines 109, 117 say "must be exactly 24 bytes" while actually asserting 30. Change the test comments to match the actual size (30 bytes). No-Justification Rule: the lying comment is wrong — fix the comment, not the code.

    2. RESOLVE sqlite_schema.rs AND semver_sip_networking.rs STUBS:
       - sqlite_schema.rs: Replace pub struct Model {} with real SeaORM entity definitions for accounts, transport_configs, client_settings, tls_configs. Add proper documentation for the Makefile migration workflow.
       - semver_sip_networking.rs: Replace pub struct Config {} with policy documentation constants and TLS info data types.
       - These are the two [::STUB::] markers that MUST RESOLVE for this ticket.

    3. ADD SAFE AudioFrameHeader SERIALIZATION HELPER:
       - Current tests use unsafe pointer casts to read header bytes. Add a safe `fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; 30]` method that manually serializes fields in big-endian order and `fn from_bytes(bytes: [u8; 30]) -> Self` for deserialization.
       - This moves unsafe code out of test code into a documented, reviewed method.
       - Function name: `to_bytes` (verb phrase: "convert header to wire-format bytes")
       - Function name: `from_bytes` (verb phrase: "construct header from wire-format bytes")

    4. SEQ FIELDS IN EVENT MODEL:
       - Investigate whether SipEvent has a seq field for event-audio correlation. If not, the event model must add it for the C063 invariant. This is a cross-module translatability concern.
       - Note: EventMeta has event_id: u64 which may serve as the sequence number. Document this relationship explicitly.

    5. FUNCTION NAMES AS VERB PHRASES:
       - Ensure all new functions use verb phrases: `validate()`, `to_bytes()`, `from_bytes()`, `load_accounts()`, `save_account()`.
       - Variables use domain concepts: `bind_addr` (not `addr`), `db_path` (not `path`), `jwt_secret` (not `secret`).
       - One function one responsibility: AuthConfig::validate() only validates — separate from ServerConfig loading.

    6. HARDCODED VALUES AS NAMED CONSTANTS:
       - DEFAULT_SIPRS_PORT = 3910 is already a named constant. Verify it's used consistently.
       - JWT expiry default (3600) is hardcoded as field default — this is acceptable as a struct Default trait impl value.
       - SQLite table names should be string constants if referenced multiple times.
       - CORS placeholder patterns should be constants if referenced.

tickets.title: Runtime Infrastructure — Command Serialization and AudioWorkerTask

contracts.precondition: Concurrency model established (P0-2): unbounded MPSC channel created, CoreReactor thread running, RuntimeHandle available
contracts.postcondition: RuntimeCommand enum defined with all 18 variants (the 12 pre-existing + P0-6 M20 ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect + 4 audio-source lifecycle AddAudioSource/RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource). Each variant carries a typed oneshot::Sender. DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command maps every variant to a backend execution closure or a dedicated reactor dispatch arm.
contracts.invariant: All PJSUA calls go through the MPSC channel — no direct FFI call outside the reactor thread. oneshot sender is resolved exactly once per command dispatch.

contracts.precondition: AudioMixer defined with: sources DashMap<u64, Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>>>>, next_source_id AtomicU64, per-source gain map, per-source muted flags
contracts.postcondition: AudioWorkerTask struct defined with spawn() (creates a Tokio blocking task), shutdown() (terminates gracefully), and a frame processing loop. Source lifecycle API defined as RuntimeCommand variants and functional through the reactor-owned AudioMixer: add_audio_source (returns source_id), remove_audio_source (removes by id), set_audio_source_gain (updates clamped gain), mute_audio_source (toggles flag).
contracts.invariant: Sources added/removed at frame boundaries — AudioWorker processes pending lifecycle commands between process_frame iterations. source_id monotonically increases (wraps correctly at u64::MAX). Concurrent add/remove does not corrupt source iteration.

contracts.precondition: AsyncAudioSource trait defined: trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; }
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> per source_id. AudioWorker calls next_chunk on each source during process_frame and pushes the mixed frame to out_queue. MockAsyncAudioSource implements AsyncAudioSource for testing.
contracts.invariant: next_chunk returns 0 for an exhausted source without panicking. next_chunk fills the buffer partially (returns < buf.len()) for end-of-stream. Implementation is Send + Sync safe.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

Six omissions were confirmed — O-001..O-006 (3 major, 3 minor). Every omission must be fully resolved, and every contract (C011, C035, C036) must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Close the ABC Inspection gaps and make the runtime infrastructure layer provably correct: (1) RuntimeCommand covers all 18 variants (incl. QueryState from P7-2, M20 ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect, and the 4 audio-source lifecycle commands), (2) RuntimeHandle exposes working audio-lifecycle submit methods that route through the reactor to a reactor-owned AudioMixer, (3) AudioWorkerTask's process_frame is test-verified end-to-end (next_chunk → gain/mute → mix → out_queue), and (4) MockBackend.conf_connect/conf_disconnect record observable side effects so the ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect dispatch path is provably wired.

### Purpose
The RuntimeCommand enum is the universal command interface that SipClient uses to drive the SIP stack. Every async public API call on SipClient eventually becomes a RuntimeCommand variant submitted via MPSC. The AudioWorkerTask enables per-call audio processing on dedicated Tokio blocking tasks, keeping audio computation off the reactor thread and the async runtime. Source lifecycle (add/remove/gain/mute) becomes a first-class RuntimeCommand capability.

### Motivation
P0-2 established the concurrency model with the base RuntimeCommand variants. P0-4 added the SipError type and M20 error converters. P0-5 added the EventBus and GetAccountInfo variant. P7-2 added QueryState. P0-6 extended the enum with M20 conference commands and the audio-source lifecycle. The ABC Inspection confirmed that although the implementation exists, the test suite does not detect regressions in the ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect dispatch path (O-001), the AudioWorker mix pipeline (O-002), or the audio-lifecycle reactor path (O-003). This re-implementation exists to close those detection gaps.

### Constraints
- Must not break existing RuntimeCommand API (backward-compatible extension).
- AudioMixer uses dashmap::DashMap (not std::sync::Mutex<HashMap>) for lock-free concurrent reads.
- AudioWorkerTask runs on Tokio blocking pool — no tokio::spawn on the reactor thread.
- No real PJSIP FFI calls in this ticket — all backend operations use MockBackend.
- AsyncAudioSource trait uses i16 (PCM S16LE), not f32 (migration is a future concern).
- The reactor must own the AudioMixer instance that audio-lifecycle commands mutate (single-writer rule on the reactor thread).
scope: **Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**

- [src/runtime/command.rs] Action: modify — RuntimeCommand already has all 18 variants (12 pre-existing + 6 P0-6 additions); verify/keep them. Before → After: DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command no longer maps RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource to Execute closures returning hardcoded Err(BackendError("audio source lifecycle not yet connected (P0-7)")) (command.rs:349-383); instead they map to new dedicated DispatchCommand variants carrying typed oneshot replies.

- [src/runtime/command.rs] Action: add — new DispatchCommand variants: RemoveAudioSource { source_id: u64, reply: oneshot::Sender<Result<(), ReactorError>> }, SetAudioSourceGain { source_id: u64, gain: f32, reply: ... }, MuteAudioSource { source_id: u64, muted: bool, reply: ... }. API: each carries the mixer-mutation payload + reply. Update Debug/Display and from_runtime_command.

- [src/runtime/handle.rs] Action: add — 4 public async submit methods: submit_add_audio_source(source: Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) -> Result<u64, ReactorError>, submit_remove_audio_source(source_id: u64) -> Result<(), ReactorError>, submit_set_audio_source_gain(source_id: u64, gain: f32) -> Result<(), ReactorError>, submit_mute_audio_source(source_id: u64, muted: bool) -> Result<(), ReactorError>. - [src/runtime/reactor.rs] Action: add — reactor owns an Arc<AudioMixer> (default-call mixer) alongside client_state. DispatchCommand::AddAudioSource arm (reactor.rs:111-123) calls mixer.add_source(source) and replies Ok(source_id). New arms for RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource call mixer.remove_source/set_gain/mute and reply Ok/Err. Before → After: the BackendError stub is replaced with real mixer routing.

- [src/runtime/backend.rs] Action: modify — MockBackend gains observable conf_connect/conf_disconnect side effects (e.g., pub conf_connect_calls: Vec<(i32, i32)> and conf_disconnect_calls: Vec<(i32, i32)> recording (source, sink)). - [Cargo.toml] Action: verify — dashmap = "6", async-trait = "0.1", crossbeam-queue = "0.3" already present; no dependency change required.

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
- Real PJSIP FFI conference-port integration (pjsua_conf_connect / pjsua_conf_disconnect) — deferred to P2-4; requires FFI binding, this ticket uses MockBackend only.
- Audio resampling, stereo/pair alignment, dynamic frame_duration — deferred to P1+ (AudioMixer is mono 8kHz 20ms i16).
- CPAL/microphone capture and real hardware audio I/O — deferred to P1-4.
- Slab-based source allocation for >32 sources — deferred to P1+ (documented future optimization).
- f32 sample-type migration of AsyncAudioSource — deferred to a future round (i16 is the current contract).
**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
- src/runtime/command.rs — DispatchCommand gains up to 3 variants; Display/Debug/from_runtime_command matches must stay exhaustive.
- src/runtime/handle.rs — public API surface gains 4 submit methods; submit() match on DispatchCommand becomes total (no unreachable!()).
- src/runtime/reactor.rs — reactor loop gains mixer-backed dispatch arms; AddAudioSource stub replaced.
- src/runtime/backend.rs — MockBackend gains observable counters; SipBackend trait unchanged (no implementor breakage).
- src/runtime/audio_worker.rs — test hook for wrap invariant; no production logic change.

[Normal condition] RuntimeCommand has 18 distinct enum discriminants, each carrying a typed oneshot::Sender; reply channels are always created at construction and replaced by RuntimeHandle::submit()'s fresh channel (never reused). [Error invariant] oneshot::Sender is always resolved (send() called) in every code path of reactor dispatch — including the panic path, which replies Err(ReactorError::BackendError) before setting terminated. tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed (7 omissions: O-001..O-007). This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round.

N0046 defines tracing spans for all public operations and the optional metrics feature. N0047 defines security (SecretString, Authorization redaction) and platform differences (Windows MSVC, macOS frameworks, Linux libs). N0050 defines the optional cpal-input feature and complete usage examples for client init, account management, calling, audio tap, and AI TTS.

### Goal
Add tracing instrumentation to all public operations, implement SecretString for credential safety, define ClientCapabilities as part of the initialization protocol, document platform-specific build requirements, provide comprehensive usage examples — and close all 7 ABC inspection gaps (O-001..O-007) confirmed in the prior implementation round.

### Purpose
Observability ensures debuggability of production SIP calls; SecretString prevents accidental credential leaks via log output (investigating an incident should never expose passwords); ClientCapabilities enables consumers to adapt their feature usage to what the runtime supports; platform documentation reduces build friction across three target OSes.

### Motivation
Without tracing, diagnosing call failures in production is guesswork. Without SecretString, any error-format! or Debug-impl on AuthCredentials leaks the password to logs. Without ClientCapabilities, consumers cannot determine at runtime whether ICE, SRTP, or a specific codec is available. The ABC inspection confirmed 7 testable behaviors that the prior implementation left untested or unimplemented: (O-001) no compile-time #[instrument] attribute-presence test; (O-002) SipClient::new never emits ClientInitialized; (O-003) metrics types not feature-gated; (O-004) no Drop zeroization for SecretString; (O-005) metrics zero-test covers only 4 of 8 defaults; (O-006) no include_str! platform-doc test; (O-007) open_default_microphone_source missing and spec-examples are empty stubs. These gaps block the first production deployment of siprs.

### Constraints
Must work with existing SipClient facade (P0-3) and EventBus (P0-5). SecretString must be zeroize-compatible but optional (behind zeroize feature). All types must be serde-compatible (behind serde feature) for WebSocket serialization (P4-4). tracing spans must not change public API signatures. cpal-input is optional and non-default. Metrics types must be structurally feature-gated (O-003). open_default_microphone_source defers real capture to the cpal crate (P8-4).

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
## Translatability improvements (Boy Scout Rule)

### 1. src/config/observability_metrics.rs — metrics feature-gating + test precision
**Current**: Metrics types compiled unconditionally; `metrics_types_not_available_without_feature` is an empty no-op (a lying test name). `metrics_registry_starts_at_zero` asserts only 4 of 8 metrics (under-specified).
**Target**: Add structural `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]` on each metrics type so the source reads as "these types exist only under the metrics feature". Replace the no-op with `metrics_types_are_feature_gated` (source-inspection asserting the cfg attribute precedes each type). Extend `metrics_registry_starts_at_zero` to name all 8 metrics — the test then reads as a complete inventory.

### 2. src/security/security_platform_diffs.rs — drop-zeroization + doc enforcement
**Current**: `impl zeroize::Zeroize` exists but drop does not zeroize (a security gap the doc comment implies is covered: "the inner memory is zeroed on drop"). The doc comment lies.
**Target**: Add `#[cfg(feature = "zeroize")] impl Drop for SecretString` so the comment becomes true; add `secret_string_zeroized_on_drop` buffer-zero test; add `platform_docs_contain_os_notes` include_str! test so the OS-specific build notes are enforced rather than decorative.

### 3. src/client.rs — ClientInitialized emission + instrument enforcement
**Current**: `SipClient::new` returns a receiver but never publishes the initialization result; the `ClientInitialized` variant is dead code. `tracing_and_metrics_specified` asserts only that Cargo.toml contains the substring 'tracing' — it cannot detect removal of `#[instrument]`.
**Target**: Publish `ClientInitialized(ClientCapabilities::new())` after Initialize succeeds so the facade reads as "construct → initialize → advertise capabilities". Add `all_public_client_methods_are_instrumented` (source-inspection) so the tracing contract is provable, replacing the substring check as the primary guard.

### 4. src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — RFC §40 API contract
**Current**: The RFC-specified `open_default_microphone_source` does not exist; examples are empty `fn main() {}` stubs that demonstrate nothing.
**Target**: Add `open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` behind `#[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")]` (typed STUB body pending cpal/P8-4) so the module reads as the audio-source entry point. Add `spec_examples_reference_public_api_types` so examples become documentation that references the real API.

### 5. Extract hardcoded feature strings into named constants
**Current**: Feature names are compared inline against string literals in tests (e.g., "cpal-input", "metrics") in client.rs and observability_metrics.rs.
**Target**: Define `const FEATURE_CPAL_INPUT: &str = "cpal-input"` and `const FEATURE_METRICS: &str = "metrics"` in a `features` constants module (or per-module consts) for test reuse — prevents drift if a feature is renamed.

contracts.invariant: 3 DTMF method categories: Inband (RFC 2833 in-band tone), SIP INFO (SipInfo in Info variant), RFC 4733 (out-of-band RTP event). DtmfPolicy always has at least one send_method and one receive_method — validated in AccountConfig::validate().

contracts.precondition: Audio subscribe uses sources — AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource+Send>; AsyncAudioSource trait defined with async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize
contracts.postcondition: AsyncAudioSource trait with RPITIT — async fn next_chunk in trait definition (currently #[async_trait] desugaring). ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derived for all T: AsyncAudioSource + Send. SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> provided for synchronous sources.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

- 【Goal】Define and implement the DTMF specification (DtmfMethod, DtmfReceivedInfo with the method:DtmfMethod field and contract-correct Option<u16>/Option<i8> field types), the AsyncAudioSource adapter types (ErasedAudioSource, SyncAudioSource, SyncSourceAdapter<T>), and the IncomingCall / REFER-transfer types (IncomingCall, IncomingCallConfig, ReferRequest.replaces, TransferInfo) per RFC nodes N0028 / N0032 / N0048. Close the 4 ABC inspection omissions (O-001..O-004) and resolve the TS-003 orphan-ticket crime in src/config/versioning_policy.rs so the ticket survives a full make → plan → start → review → resolve cycle this time.
- 【Purpose】Provide type-safe DTMF signalling primitives for SIP call control (send + receive with DtmfPolicy validation). Enable downstream crates to implement custom async audio sources for AudioMixer via the SyncAudioSource → SyncSourceAdapter bridge and the ErasedAudioSource dynamic-dispatch wrapper. Expose incoming call metadata (from_uri, to_uri, display_name, headers, offered_codecs, has_early_media) and REFER-based transfer capabilities (ReferRequest.replaces, TransferCompleted) to application code as typed SipEventPayload variants.
- 【Motivation】The ABC Inspection Pipeline remanded P8-4 with one critical omission (O-001: ReferRequest.replaces missing and zero tests construct ReferRequest/TransferInfo, so the C049 invariant and acceptance criteria are unenforced), one major (O-002: DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms widened to Option<u64> and volume_dbm0 to Option<i32> vs the contract Option<u16>/Option<i8>, and no None/0/MAX edge tests), and two minor (O-003: no SipEventPayload::DtmfSent construction test; O-004: no 65536-sample SyncAudioSource boundary test). The versioning_policy.rs STUB (TS-003) is an orphaned ticket reference that must be resolved this round. Every contract (C029/C030/C033/C049) must be translated into precise test assertions so that removing any contract behavior fails a test.
- 【Constraints】MSRV 1.95 — RPITIT is stable but the existing AsyncAudioSource uses #[async_trait] for Box<dyn> compatibility in AudioMixer; the ErasedAudioSource blanket impl provides the dynamic-dispatch path without refactoring existing implementors. Do NOT add new crate dependencies — all required derives (Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq) are std. Keep the canonical 4-variant DtmfMethod (Rfc2833, Rfc4733, Info, Inband) from account_config_spec.rs; leave the separate 2-variant DtmfMethod in m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs intact to avoid breaking DtmfSentInfo consumers (unification is an open item, not a forced change). Maintain backward compatibility with existing DtmfReceivedInfo consumers (m20_native_event_conv.rs constructs with None/None, so field-type narrowing is compatible). ReferRequest gains the additive replaces: Option<String> field; all struct-literal construction sites must add it.

ReferRequest gains the additive replaces: Option<String> field. VersionPolicy is a new public type in the config domain. No changes to the AsyncAudioSource / ErasedAudioSource / SyncAudioSource / SyncSourceAdapter signatures (already present from P5-2/P0-6).

Non-change (item): PJSIP FFI callback wiring (on_dtmf_digit / on_incoming_call / on_refer) and the Reactor event dispatch — separate P5-3 ticket. RPITIT refactoring of the existing #[async_trait] AsyncAudioSource — deferred. Attended transfer end-to-end (REFER with Replaces targeting a live call) — depends on the multi-call state machine, P5-3+. Unification of the 2-variant DtmfMethod with the 4-variant canonical — open item, not forced.

Non-change (why): The P8-4 scope is the pure type definitions + test assertions that close the ABC gaps. FFI wiring needs a live PJSIP stack; RPITIT refactor risks the working AudioMixer integration; attended transfer needs multi-call semantics; DtmfMethod unification would break DtmfSentInfo consumers (P7-2 tests). Each is a separate, larger change better owned by a dedicated ticket.

Impact (component): src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs — event payload structs (DtmfReceivedInfo, ReferRequest) + SipEventPayload variants. src/config/versioning_policy.rs — new VersionPolicy type (additive). src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — test-only change + STUB re-scope. src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs — DtmfReceivedInfo construction (None-compatible). runtime/audio_worker consumers — ErasedAudioSource blanket impl adds an impl boundary with zero migration cost.

Impact (nature): API surface expansion (additive: replaces field, VersionPolicy) + field-type narrowing (minor breaking for DtmfReceivedInfo literal constructors). Existing Default implementations and None-construction paths remain compatible. No behavioral change to event dispatch.

Impact (response): Downstream crates constructing DtmfReceivedInfo must pass Option<u16>/Option<i8> values (u64/i32 literals beyond the range fail to compile — intended, enforces the boundary invariant). ReferRequest constructors must add replaces: Option<String>. VersionPolicy is additive with no consumer impact.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvement plan (Boy Scout Rule — leave code cleaner than found):
- Function names as verb phrases: DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed already read as verbs — keep. VersionPolicy methods must be verbs: classify_change(), requires_changelog(), current_phase() — never generic names like process() or check().
- Variable names as domain concepts: DtmfReceivedInfo fields already use SIP domain terms (method, digit, duration_ms, volume_dbm0). ReferRequest.replaces is the domain term for the Replaces header — no generic option. VersionPolicy must name the semver concepts (phase, change_kind, changelog) not raw strings.
- One function one responsibility: VersionPolicy::classify_change answers only "what kind of change" — CHANGELOG gating is a separate method requires_changelog(). Do not merge classification with release automation.
- Hardcoded values as named constants: DEFAULT_AUTO_REJECT_TIMEOUT_MS (incoming_call_refer.rs:36) and DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS (m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:64) already exist — keep. Any new versioning thresholds become named constants in versioning_policy.rs.
- No error swallowing: AccountConfig::validate errors propagate via ?. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes errors on the EventBus instead of log-and-continue. VersionPolicy returns typed errors for invalid classifications.
- Proactive cleanups in touched files: update the stale [::STUB::] P0-1 reference in versioning_policy.rs (resolved by implementation); re-scope the microphone STUB to MUST RESOLVE with the cpal constraint reason instead of leaving a misleading P8-4 reference that would later read as a completed-ticket staleness crime; in event_model_payload_bus.rs, align the DtmfReceivedInfo doc comment with the narrowed Option<u16>/Option<i8> types and add the replaces field doc to ReferRequest.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal (original)
Establish the siprs crate's public identity as a safe asynchronous SIP audio client library. Define SipClient as the top-level facade that integrates with P0-2's CoreReactor/RuntimeHandle/RuntimeCommand infrastructure.

### Purpose (original)
Provide Rust application code with a safe, async-native facade over PJSUA SIP functionality, limited to audio-only voice communication. This crate exists to eliminate unsafe FFI boilerplate and deliver SIP calling capabilities through idiomatic Rust APIs — Result propagation, tokio async/await, typed events, and structured configuration.

### Motivation (original)
P0-3 is the gateway ticket that establishes the crate's architectural identity before downstream tickets implement specific sub-systems: error types (P0-4), event system (P0-5), FFI layer (P0-6), audio pipeline (P1+). Without a defined SipClient + ClientConfig, no downstream implementation has a cohesive host. This ticket crystallizes the purpose defined in RFC 1 (§1) into concrete public API surface.

### Constraints (original)
- Audio-only: no video API surface (RFC §1, §2). Enforced by compile-time assertions.
- All async public APIs must return Result<T, SipError> (RFC §1 constraint on N0001).
- PJSIP v2.x via FFI only — no raw socket-level SIP stack.
- Single crate with modular internal structure (RFC §6, C009).
- Shutdown must be cancellation-safe and idempotent (RFC §32, C044).
- SecretString for password storage (RFC §35-36, C048).
- Microphone input is optional via cpal-input feature flag (RFC §40, C051).
- MSRV 1.95, OS targets per RFC §4 (C006).

### Goal (re-implementation round)
Make the crate identity verifiable and regression-proof: the facade `SipClient` + `ClientConfig` must exist as typed, validated, audio-only API surface, and the test suite must detect any violation of the 15 RFC §1 contracts. Concretely: all four ABC findings (O-001 `assert_sync::<SipClient>()`, O-002 `metrics` feature presence, O-003 `tls`/`srtp` independence, O-004 `std::thread::JoinHandle<()>` type assertion) are closed by new test assertions, and `make test` stays green (baseline 647 unit + 37 integration + 1 doc-test).

### Purpose (why this exists)
The crate exists to eliminate unsafe PJSUA FFI boilerplate and deliver SIP voice calling through idiomatic Rust — `Result<T, SipError>` propagation, tokio async/await, typed events, structured configuration. This ticket defines and locks the crate's public identity so downstream tickets (P0-4 error, P0-5 event, P0-6 FFI, P1+ audio) have a stable host. The ABC round re-confirms that identity through precise test assertions rather than broad ones.

### Motivation (why now)
The ABC Inspection Pipeline (criteria A contract-translation, B violation-detection, C test-precision) found 4 violations in the prior P0-3 implementation: the `Sync` half of `SipClient: Send + Sync` was unenforced (O-001), `metrics` feature presence was untested (O-002), tls/srtp feature independence was untested (O-003), and the `std::thread` reactor model was not type-pinned (O-004). These are regression gaps, not new features: without them, future refactors could silently break the crate identity. This ticket is remanded to close the gaps and re-verify all 15 contracts.

### Constraints (re-implementation round boundaries)
- Audio-only: no video API surface (RFC §1/§2, C001 invariant) — enforced by compile-time tests.
- All async public APIs return `Result<T, SipError>` (RFC §1, N0001 global invariant).
- PJSIP v2.x (pinned 2.17, RFC §4) via FFI only; no raw socket-level SIP stack.
- Single crate, modular internal structure (RFC §6, C009 invariant).
- Shutdown cancellation-safe and idempotent (RFC §32, C044 invariant).
- `SecretString` (zeroize) for password storage (RFC §35-36, C048 invariant).
- Microphone optional via `cpal-input` feature (RFC §40, C051 invariant).
- MSRV 1.95; OS targets Windows x86_64, macOS arm64, Ubuntu x86_64 (RFC §4, C006 invariant).
- No new dependencies and no public API changes in this round — test-hardening only.

Type signature under test: `pub async fn new(config: ClientConfig) -> Result<(Self, broadcast::Receiver<SipEvent>), SipError>`. Verifies C001 precondition (RFC defines purpose → valid config accepted), C002 precondition (concurrency model defined → reactor spawns).

Verifies the event-facing surface is wired to `EventBus` (C047 observability precondition).
- UT: [Normal] `sip_client_shutdown_completes` — `client.shutdown().await` completes inside a 5s `tokio::time::timeout`; afterwards `client.is_terminated() == true`. Verifies C044 postcondition (shutdown with cancellation safety).

Verifies C001 precondition.
- UT: [Normal] `client_config_default_user_agent_contains_version` — default `user_agent` starts with `siprs/` and embeds `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` (currently `0.1.0`).
